<span id="paper-agent-research-strategist-e4eab6e6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e13afb92bd736c7">Does Strategist accumulate model parameters, the current answer, or another cross-task asset?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astrategist">Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It freezes executor models and represents reasoning programs as Python blueprints with one execute interface. After evaluation, they enter a cross-task library with measurement cards and training-trace experience. Task prompts are separate from structure; later tasks can compose or reuse structures. This is neither gradient training nor merely editing the current answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: a discovered procedure that creates three candidates and reviews them independently can be retested with new prompts in another domain. Saving one problem&#x27;s final number is not reusable blueprint accumulation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03618">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.03618-strategist/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e13afb92bd736c7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:strategist" data-paper-title="Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-47c56ce966b3f834">Do exactly two percentage points of accuracy gain and exactly 2% lower cost automatically satisfy Strategist&#x27;s win rule?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astrategist">Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Improvement requires more than two percentage points or a cost ratio strictly below 0.98; the other metric must remain within its tolerance band. The candidate must win on validation and hidden, then ranks by hidden accuracy gain and cost ratio. The default rule is not a confidence test, even though standard errors are computed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: d=0.02 and cost ratio 0.98 are ties. d=0 and ratio 0.97 can be a cost win, but a three-percentage-point hidden accuracy loss still prevents selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与实现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03618">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.03618-strategist/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47c56ce966b3f834">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:strategist" data-paper-title="Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e88e95c2628b4d5">Both Strategist and EvalAlloc inspect candidate measurements. Do they optimize the same object?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astrategist">Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Strategist proposes and composes executable reasoning strategies, retaining structures and experience for later tasks. EvalAlloc mainly determines which SEARCH evaluation cells to execute, how shared references estimate fitness, and how final confirmation works. Cheap observations or high predicted scores do not generate better strategies, and library admission does not establish held-out success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: evaluating 100 fewer items changes the observation budget. Replacing direct answering with a reusable decomposition-and-review program changes strategy structure. They can be combined, but costs and real held-out success need separate records.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地结果与负控, 高成本完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03618">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.03618-strategist/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4e88e95c2628b4d5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:strategist" data-paper-title="Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<h2 id="qa-cc71f470d55ad83b">Why do passing AST, DAG, and paired-pick tests not establish a complete Strategist or Evolve integration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astrategist">Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The module calls no designer or executor model; retrieval scores and candidate evaluations are supplied externally. Explicit prompt elision is only a structural fingerprint, not proof about helper semantics or dynamic dependencies. Paired-pick does not isolate hidden data within a Python process. Actual proposal, execution, retrieval, and information-flow isolation require separate acceptance. The present CPU diagnostic is not promotion-eligible capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: synthetic arms with accuracy 0.7 and costs 10 and 8 verify ratio 0.8 and fallback behavior. No model has answered a question, and cross-task search has not been demonstrated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 数据协议与实现边界, 本地结果与负控, 代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03618">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.03618-strategist/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cc71f470d55ad83b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsi-opt" data-paper-title="RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-rsi-opt-94e59e6e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-066ae36575676705">Why does RSI-Opt improve optimization methods instead of only optimizing one fixed model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-opt">RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An update that works now may fail on other models or stages. RSI-Opt treats the updater as the evolving object, evaluates controlled runs, and decides what to keep. Distinguish inner optimization from outer method selection. Candidate prose or one strong score does not establish broad gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Train a small model with one rule, then compare rules under equal budgets rather than retain one run&#x27;s best weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32026v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.32026-rsi-opt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-066ae36575676705">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsi-opt" data-paper-title="RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d4432df8e608d4f4">Why hide final metrics from the inner agent while letting the outer loop evaluate strategy with them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-opt">RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The inner agent edits an updater from training loss and diagnostics. Final metrics would let it tune directly against evaluation. The outer loop compares fixed strategy outcomes and has a different selection role. Inherited prompts, libraries, and cadence make it recursive; normalized rankings are not unseen-task generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Tune update rules from training loss; compare strategies after execution rather than inspect test scores for every edit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32026v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.32026-rsi-opt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d4432df8e608d4f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsi-opt" data-paper-title="RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-24437c49b12176e9">Why fix model, data order, and update budget across candidates rather than only seed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-opt">RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Changing architecture, loss, or duration confounds updater effects. A fixed contract controls the optimization problem, and failed updater trials can roll back. Multiple seeds do not repair systematic protocol differences or make training-suite scores generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A gets ten thousand steps and B gets a thousand. The same seed does not attribute their score difference to the updater.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32026v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.32026-rsi-opt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24437c49b12176e9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsi-opt" data-paper-title="RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-74594fbd5fa19d33">What are the evidence limits of archiving low-score descendants and removing exposed branches?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-opt">RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Archive evaluated low-score strategies to preserve failed exploration rather than fake monotonic progress. Removing a branch exposed to held-out descriptions may not remove summaries read by other descendants. The paper leaves that provenance issue open. Z-score aggregation is not significance testing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Deleting a contaminated policy while retaining summaries based on it can still leak to descendants.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32026v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.32026-rsi-opt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-74594fbd5fa19d33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:image-rsi" data-paper-title="ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-image-rsi-f8d5a27f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-33b4f94f521f4a4c">Why do fixed original requirements matter more than increasing a five-axis average?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aimage-rsi">ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Repair must meet original counts, relationships, wording, and identity constraints. It cannot discard difficult conditions or average away failures. Five dimensions diagnose issues; hard vetoes govern acceptance. A high score does not guarantee image facts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Beauty cannot compensate for two cups when three and correct text were required. Do not change the request to two or three.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32120v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.32120-image-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-33b4f94f521f4a4c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:image-rsi" data-paper-title="ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f8c753569fbafcbc">Why can&#x27;t a high in-loop image score automatically activate an extracted strategy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aimage-rsi">ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A judge that guides repairs and scores their gains can amplify its biases. Compare with and without experience at matching request, configuration, and seed; calibrate with independent blinded judgments and admit on a held-out set. Hard constraints cannot be averaged away. Returning a fallback is not acceptance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A strategy improves composition to please the judge but misses the required person count. Independent matched tests and vetoes expose this.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32120v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.32120-image-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f8c753569fbafcbc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:image-rsi" data-paper-title="ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ae7e526e94592742">Why separate experience extraction from independent paired admission?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aimage-rsi">ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A strategy inferred from a trajectory is only a candidate. Compare with and without it under matched request, input, configuration, and seed, then blind-calibrate and use independent holdout. In-loop judges may favor their own guidance; test verdicts must not guide generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Stronger spatial wording works on one image. Pair on new requests to see if it harms other relations or styles before admitting it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32120v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.32120-image-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ae7e526e94592742">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:image-rsi" data-paper-title="ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-132ef279c0c873ba">Does returning the highest-scoring fallback after two repairs mean accepted?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aimage-rsi">ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The best of the initial image and up to two repairs may be returned even if all fail hard constraints. Judge SFT/GRPO updates between collection rounds, not within one evaluation request. Local generation, semantic judging, and training are unimplemented, so formulas are not system verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If all three images misspell required text, the prettiest fallback still fails the checklist.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32120v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.32120-image-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-132ef279c0c873ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessmm" data-paper-title="HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harnessmm-efa1b75e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f97e11482fc1d08">Why can another model call after tool feedback repeat an already completed decision in HarnessMM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessmm">HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The prior turn can decide a later command while waiting for a prerequisite. Once a guard holds, another reasoning call may add nothing. HarnessMM reuses committed decisions to avoid slow calls, but genuinely new interpretation goes back to the model. Reuse is not arbitrary future prediction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If a specified test should follow successful file creation, trigger it from the receipt. An unexpected error needs new reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32813v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.32813-harnessmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f97e11482fc1d08">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessmm" data-paper-title="HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f0cd3e3e41dc248b">Why do closed arguments and true guards not prove a skipped model call was correct and actually avoided?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessmm">HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They show an action can be reused, not that it completes the task; the original evaluator still judges semantics. Execution certificates must bind exact arguments, predecessor receipts, and tool outputs, and audit that the registered slow call did not occur. Theoretical savings differ from actual calls; include failures and recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Directly run a saved test command, keep the receipt, and verify no extra slow model request before counting a saving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32813v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.32813-harnessmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f0cd3e3e41dc248b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessmm" data-paper-title="HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a00533c8b214ed6">How does reusing a fixed action differ in online freedom from planning a new action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessmm">HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reuse is limited to previously resolved actions with complete arguments and satisfied guards. It cannot invent steps or fill parameters from new evidence. Planning interprets observations and constructs actions. Reuse saves repetition only where covered; otherwise abstain. Structural success is not semantic correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A saved test command can trigger on success. A new dependency conflict cannot be fixed by guessing a command in the reuser.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32813v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.32813-harnessmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a00533c8b214ed6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessmm" data-paper-title="HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-403e05ae2ac0edb4">Why include failures, fallbacks, and development in HarnessMM cost accounting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessmm">HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An episode counts all real input and output tokens: structure generation, selection, extra context, recovery, and final synthesis, including cached input. Record development separately and amortize over deployments. One fewer slow call does not guarantee lower total tokens, latency, or energy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Saving one main-model call but adding two selection/recovery calls requires counting all. Amortize graph construction over actual reuse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32813v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.32813-harnessmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-403e05ae2ac0edb4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:oo-harness" data-paper-title="Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-oo-harness-cd6587e9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-001a95d0b85c9840">Why use inheritable harness classes for specialization across tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aoo-harness">Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A generic flow may not suit every task, while copying whole implementations loses shared verified logic. Classes express reusable behavior and overrides, then route tasks to suitable variants. Inheritance organizes code and does not add runtime agents or guarantee universal improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A browsing subclass reuses recovery and changes search. Selecting it executes one flow, not parent and child separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.28380-oo-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-001a95d0b85c9840">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:oo-harness" data-paper-title="Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5d4d6c07f614cbe3">Why doesn&#x27;t inheriting a parent harness method mean running several ancestor agents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aoo-harness">Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Inheritance reuses code: one instance invokes a non-overridden parent method, without separate ancestor trajectories. A subclass changes only needed hooks; deployment selects one frozen class. Cluster gains do not guarantee global gains, and self-confidence ablations are not calibrated success probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Override the search prompt while retaining the parent&#x27;s terminal implementation. That is one agent, not two parallel collaborators.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.28380-oo-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5d4d6c07f614cbe3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:oo-harness" data-paper-title="Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-67c269161e84e1cc">What is the trade-off between strict target-cluster admission and one global mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aoo-harness">Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The target cluster must strictly beat its current specialist and pass extra checks, so a global mean cannot hide a local regression. This does not guarantee gains elsewhere. Routing uses public tasks and observed base traces, not test grader scores. Self-reported 0.7 is uncalibrated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Validate a spreadsheet-specific change on spreadsheets. Gains on an easier unrelated cluster cannot mask no improvement there.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.28380-oo-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67c269161e84e1cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:oo-harness" data-paper-title="Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c54046ce9413a3c7">Why must a specialized class start in the same initial environment, whereas selecting Base can reuse its result?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aoo-harness">Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Base runs before routing, so its existing result can be used if it is ultimately selected. A specialized class must reset through tool_factory so that it does not inherit Base&#x27;s progress. Real external effects are not guaranteed to roll back. Trusted local Python classes and allowlisted data isolation are not a security sandbox, and a scripted actor does not demonstrate LLM capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If Base has already created half the files, letting a specialist continue would make it look more successful. A fair comparison starts from the same initial file state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.28380-oo-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c54046ce9413a3c7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-s4" data-paper-title="Evolving Agent Interfaces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agent-s4-640f2b45" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5b57cb78fed3749">How does evolving the interface differ from accumulating skills composed from existing tools?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-s4">Evolving Agent Interfaces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Skills generally combine procedures over a fixed action and observation interface. S4 lets a Meta-Agent change interface code and usage knowledge, changing what the task agent can see and do. The task model and harness are held fixed to isolate the interface effect, but a new interface still needs execution on real tasks; renaming the repository version is not enough.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Replacing cell-by-cell editing with bulk operations over a region changes the interface. Recording that cells should be sorted before editing is usage knowledge for the existing tool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28601">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.28601-agent-s4/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5b57cb78fed3749">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-s4" data-paper-title="Evolving Agent Interfaces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-290fc521db43089d">Why retain a temporarily low-scoring child interface repository in the population rather than keeping only changes that strictly improve on their parents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-s4">Evolving Agent Interfaces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Evolutionary search may have to pass through local valleys or combine different changes. Retaining descendants lets later mutation and crossover reuse their structure. Validation scores guide parent selection, but validation traces and labels are not exposed to the Meta-Agent. What evolves is the action and observation interface itself; the search is not greedy acceptance of the best patch in each round.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An interface change may perform modestly on its own but work well with observation compression from another lineage. Immediately discarding all low-scoring children eliminates that opportunity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28601">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.28601-agent-s4/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-290fc521db43089d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-s4" data-paper-title="Evolving Agent Interfaces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4a95f794a9b3ec9">How do single-parent mutation and two-parent crossover differ in where they get their changes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-s4">Evolving Agent Interfaces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mutation modifies the interface and usage knowledge of a single parent. Crossover combines structures or experience from two different parents. Both construct candidates from unlabeled training traces; private validation outcomes are used only for population selection, not handed to the Meta-Agent as answers. Crossover broadens the available combinations but can introduce incompatibilities, so freeze the resulting child before independently evaluating it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One parent improves screenshot observations and another improves bulk editing. Crossover can attempt both, whereas single-parent mutation works from just one current repository.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28601">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.28601-agent-s4/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4a95f794a9b3ec9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-s4" data-paper-title="Evolving Agent Interfaces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e85d3ecb46446354">Why does BuilderContext omit validation diagnostics, and why does low-score pruning retain lineage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-s4">Evolving Agent Interfaces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Validation is used only to select parents. Passing diagnostics would turn a protected selection set into development feedback. Pruning revokes parent eligibility while retaining audit history and final candidates, including failures. The local controller uses trusted callbacks and synthetic tasks; it neither executes arbitrary interface source nor demonstrates improvement in a real GUI.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the Meta-Agent sees filenames from validation failures and fixes them directly, it is no longer developing from the permitted training traces. Deleting low-scoring records would also conceal the cost of search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28601">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.28601-agent-s4/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e85d3ecb46446354">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aptamer-lab-loop" data-paper-title="Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-aptamer-lab-loop-d80e05ef" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f037abf7dbe5b196">Why should aptamer design repeatedly connect computational proposals to real experimental feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaptamer-lab-loop">Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A computational model estimates candidate properties from existing data; actual molecular behavior may depend on factors it did not model. This work uses real measurements to test proposals and inform the next round, making experimentation rather than a predicted score the decisive feedback. Changing candidates and selection conditions across rounds means progress in the loop does not automatically demonstrate stronger performance on a fixed test set.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a candidate favored by the model performs modestly when measured, use the counterexample in the next round. Raising its predicted score does not alter the physical measurement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24806v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.24806-aptamer-lab-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f037abf7dbe5b196">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aptamer-lab-loop" data-paper-title="Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-356a38d089051a53">Why can&#x27;t high computational-proxy scores replace real experimental feedback, or be compared across rounds as fixed-test gains?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaptamer-lab-loop">Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Computational scores can disagree with physical measurements. The point of the loop is that new measurements can refute predictions and preserve evidence of failures. Candidates and strategies differ across rounds, and hit rates depend on the selected distribution, so these are not directly comparable machine-learning scores on the same test set. The work assesses research orchestration and does not imply specific laboratory procedures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one round tests only the proxy&#x27;s favorite candidates and the next focuses on exploration, different hit rates may reflect selection rather than improved generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制与评测. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aptamer-lab-loop" data-paper-title="Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c4f29aea97ea8cba">What information is added by a new physical measurement versus repeated reanalysis of existing experimental records?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaptamer-lab-loop">Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reanalysis may improve interpretation or candidate selection but creates no new physical observation. A new measurement tests a previously unverified candidate and may expose model omissions. Both can support research, but recomputation is not an independent experiment and a simulated proxy cannot replace the experimental endpoint. For cross-round comparisons, preserve changes in candidates and measurement conditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reranking ten existing results still leaves ten measurements. Testing an eleventh candidate adds a genuinely new piece of external feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24806v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.24806-aptamer-lab-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c4f29aea97ea8cba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aptamer-lab-loop" data-paper-title="Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-05aefca653b2f5bd">Why doesn&#x27;t the local record replace the physical endpoint with simulated measurements or predicted scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaptamer-lab-loop">Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Real experiments can falsify the computational proxy, a defining feature that would disappear if they were replaced. The local entry documents research orchestration and cost only; it includes no model, GPU receipt, capability metric, or Evolve integration. A numeric fixture cannot stand in for a specialized laboratory or feedback that takes days, and no experimental operating procedure is provided.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Randomly generating a &#x27;measurement passed&#x27; label can test a messaging interface, but does not establish physical efficacy or complete an experimental loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心机制与评测, 本地复现与成本决策. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24806v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.24806-aptamer-lab-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-05aefca653b2f5bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:terminal-rsi" data-paper-title="Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-terminal-rsi-d5ceabe6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee2baf6e22e38c51">Why do long terminal-agent tasks present a harder reinforcement-learning feedback problem than single-turn answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aterminal-rsi">Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Hy Frontier / National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal tasks include commands, long observations, and state changes across turns. Success is often known only at the end, making it hard to assign credit to early actions; failure may also come just short of completion. Terminal RSI structures rewards and advantages around this interaction to support continued training. Partial progress is not completion, and observation length is not a direct measure of interaction time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An agent fixes the code but never runs the final test. A terminal failure label alone hides useful earlier actions; training should use evidence of progress without relaxing the completion standard.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22192-terminal-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee2baf6e22e38c51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:terminal-rsi" data-paper-title="Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b604c93ca728c134">Why does TB-GAE decay by interaction turn rather than observation text length?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aterminal-rsi">Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Hy Frontier / National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Longer tool output does not imply more elapsed decision steps. Treating a long observation as many recurrence nodes would arbitrarily over-discount credit for earlier actions. Recurrence runs only over generated tokens, with no decay within a turn and discounting across turns. Chunk continuation requires both value and advantage; a computational boundary is not an environment termination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two commands can produce the same outcome with ten lines or a thousand lines of logging. Verbosity alone should not reduce earlier actions&#x27; reward credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22192-terminal-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b604c93ca728c134">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:terminal-rsi" data-paper-title="Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-21c071abd587613f">Why do SPR and the plain partial-score FDR method rank outcomes differently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aterminal-rsi">Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Hy Frontier / National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>FDR scales partial scores by a family divisor and has no fixed upper bound, so a high-partial-score failure can outrank a success. SPR adds strict success and constrains the partial component below one, keeping failures below strict successes. This ranking property is not a proof about policy-gradient variance or potential invariance, and the paper&#x27;s overall training gains cannot be attributed to this formula alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high-scoring incomplete attempt can exceed one with FDR. With SPR, it stays below the minimum score of any strict success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22192-terminal-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21c071abd587613f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:terminal-rsi" data-paper-title="Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-888eaed3118a74ba">Why isn&#x27;t a value bootstrap alone enough when GAE is computed in chunks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aterminal-rsi">Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Hy Frontier / National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A chunk boundary does not terminate the environment. Pass both the next value and next advantage to retain the tail of the trace; emit terminal reward only once. Observations are excluded from the recurrence. The local implementation is a numeric operator without actor, critic, RSR, or real terminal training. Equivalence in the unit-clock case does not show that TB-GAE was deployed online.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the tail advantage is reset after splitting at the eleventh generated token, credit from later rewards no longer propagates backward equivalently, even with a correct next value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射、成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22192-terminal-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-888eaed3118a74ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsiflow" data-paper-title="RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-rsiflow-bf0996bb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e83fc8ef79fc5a35">Why does RSIFlow first diagnose what kind of object is responsible when automated research fails?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsiflow">RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Poor results can stem from the model, the execution process, or a defect in the current artifact. Always editing prompts or always retraining would misallocate resources. RSIFlow uses execution evidence to select an intervention related to the failure. Both the diagnosis and the candidate need actual verification: choosing a branch does not show that its bottleneck was resolved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fix the artifact if its output file has the wrong format; change the harness if the tool flow repeatedly omits verification. Neither necessarily requires retraining model weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21791-rsiflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e83fc8ef79fc5a35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsiflow" data-paper-title="RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8c0705993316eab7">Why must all RSIFlow candidates start from the same frozen parent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsiflow">RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If the first candidate&#x27;s changes leak into the second, improvements cannot be attributed to the selected Model, Harness, or Artifacts intervention. A shared parent and task batch provide a paired baseline. Only valid, strictly improving candidates are accepted; after a failure, retry from the original parent. Skills may come from training experience, but report-set scores must not leak into maintenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Evaluate a prompt change and a model replacement separately against the same parent, rather than attributing the cumulative improvement of the second run to the model alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21791-rsiflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8c0705993316eab7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsiflow" data-paper-title="RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3635aa173e7ccab2">What layer of future execution does each Model, Harness, or Artifacts intervention change?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsiflow">RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Model interventions target the model; Harness interventions change how execution is organized; Artifacts interventions act on deliverables. Their scopes and inherited state differ. Comparisons must state what changed: a one-off file fix is not general policy learning, and out-of-scope changes cannot be mixed into the designated branch. The local variant uses trusted callbacks and skill memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fixing one report changes only that artifact. Changing a check that runs on every task may affect future tasks, but transfer still needs verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21791-rsiflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3635aa173e7ccab2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsiflow" data-paper-title="RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7df2699c3716bd8a">Does a CPU controller with trusted callbacks demonstrate that full RSIFlow is integrated with Evolve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsiflow">RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The callbacks and structural evidence verify parent protection, paired acceptance, failure retention, and separation of training from reporting. There is no built-in LLM, arbitrary program execution, or six-benchmark training. Declared edit scopes and high numerical fixture scores cannot replace real candidate execution and promotion evaluation, and the in-process interface is not a sandbox for malicious code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A scalar proposer that changes one number and improves a score shows that a controller branch is reachable. It does not show that real model parameters or a harness were updated as in the paper.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射、成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21791-rsiflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7df2699c3716bd8a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auto-sft" data-paper-title="AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-auto-sft-e69c4a3b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d12282618b9c1d0">Why does AutoSFT make the selection and organization of training data an object of automated research?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauto-sft">AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different data contents, quality levels, and combinations can produce different capabilities from the same base, while manually trying many recipes is costly. AutoSFT proposes and tests data hypotheses rather than changing a training hyperparameter once. To understand a data change, control training conditions and isolate evaluation; rising development scores do not establish final generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If formatting errors may stem from a shortage of examples, add those examples and compare from the same base. Reusing previous-round weights introduces extra training history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式：固定训练合同的形式化. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22194-auto-sft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d12282618b9c1d0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auto-sft" data-paper-title="AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f387b0e8c600a749">Why is retraining from the same base each round important for attributing the effects of data research?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauto-sft">AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>This makes cross-round changes primarily attributable to the data pool, mix, and order, rather than cumulative learning from the previous round&#x27;s weights. Fix the trainer and budget and register intervention hypotheses to compare whether the predicted mechanisms appear. Proposals from different analytical views are not completed experiments, and predictions must not be rewritten after seeing the scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If round two repairs examples with incorrect answers, retrain from the same base. Continuing from round one&#x27;s weights would confound the change with extra optimization steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式：固定训练合同的形式化. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22194-auto-sft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f387b0e8c600a749">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auto-sft" data-paper-title="AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d4811813cf908dd5">How do four analytical views differ from a single agent adjusting only dataset proportions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauto-sft">AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Data, failures, training signals, and past research provide different evidence. Execution subagents return traceable artifacts and the Meta Agent chooses interventions beyond changing the mixture. The authors&#x27; six action categories were identified retrospectively rather than used as a fixed menu; a table of rule-based options is not open-ended data research.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failure analysis may suggest correcting answers, while training signals point to ordering. Compare the two proposals using evidence, rather than increasing one category&#x27;s share by five percentage points every round.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式：固定训练合同的形式化. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22194-auto-sft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d4811813cf908dd5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auto-sft" data-paper-title="AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
