<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a3c27f91439eca03">Why preregister hypotheses before training, and why retain an independent external holdout after decontamination?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauto-sft">AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Record the change, control, expected direction, and evidence in advance to prevent rewriting predictions after the fact. Repeatedly using the same evaluation failures and choosing the best score can adapt to that evaluation even without direct n-gram duplication. Only a separate, frozen holdout offers a distinct test of generalization. The local project did not run the eight-H800 training or the paid research campaign and supplies no simulated training metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the score increases but the predicted evidence does not appear, report that the hypothesis was not confirmed. Do not revise the earlier prediction to match the outcome.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式：固定训练合同的形式化, 成本决策与本地状态. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22194-auto-sft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a3c27f91439eca03">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:athanor" data-paper-title="Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-athanor-3414bb2a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7110f2236cddb02d">What is the role of separating the research agent from the asynchronous training and evaluation service?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aathanor">Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The agent selects data, algorithms, and stages. The service trains, decontaminates, runs frozen evaluation, and saves checkpoint lineage, connecting proposals to real artifacts. Separation also helps restrict access to the final held-out set. Development scores returned by the service remain noisy and are not the true performance of every proposal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After the agent proposes self-distillation, wait for the service to complete and record the new checkpoint and evaluation. A proposal saying &#x27;expected to improve&#x27; is not an outcome.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21055">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21055-athanor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7110f2236cddb02d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:athanor" data-paper-title="Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2fa991bc91763fd2">Why does an independent training service also need frozen evaluation and checkpoint lineage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aathanor">Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Asynchronous experiments produce many combinations of data, algorithms, and stages, which filenames alone cannot identify. Lineage makes parent-child relations traceable, frozen evaluation limits drift as search progresses, and a final held-out set isolates the researcher&#x27;s selection. A single highest development score can be noise, not evidence of robust capability gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For a model that underwent SFT, merging, and then self-distillation, missing parent checkpoints make it difficult to explain which intervention changed the score or to reproduce the candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21055">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21055-athanor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2fa991bc91763fd2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:athanor" data-paper-title="Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2f6eb0573de3da89">If external teachers are prohibited, how does self-distillation differ from using a stronger commercial teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aathanor">Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Self-distillation uses permitted models and existing data within the system. An external teacher introduces additional capability, cost, and data provenance, violating the research contract. A commercial model may power the research agent, but its answers must not be slipped into training labels. Keep research control separate from supervision of the model being trained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A commercial agent may plan the next round, but adding its high-quality solutions directly to the dataset no longer satisfies the no-external-teacher setting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21055">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21055-athanor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2f6eb0573de3da89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:athanor" data-paper-title="Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d66143f49b76710f">Why can&#x27;t the highest development score found during search serve as the final formal result?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aathanor">Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Selecting the maximum over repeated proposals on a noisy development set introduces selection bias. Formal comparisons must distinguish the campaign, submitted multi-seed averages, and reevaluation under consistent decoding; the final held-out set is hidden from researchers. The local entry is a literature and cost review only, with no automated research run, model execution, or GPU receipt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One chance high score in a hundred evaluations does not establish a checkpoint&#x27;s expected ability. Freeze selection and reevaluate under an independent protocol.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21055">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21055-athanor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d66143f49b76710f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:torsi" data-paper-title="The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-torsi-cd7ddf6f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-814a0e85a5594988">Why might a real-time agent reason better but still act incorrectly because it responds too slowly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atorsi">The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Samsung Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The environment keeps changing during inference, so an action based on an old observation can be stale by execution. TORSI studies improving a small execution policy under real-time constraints without putting all high-quality guidance on the online critical path. Account for offline learning and online response separately; static accuracy is not effective action in a live environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A model spends a long time choosing a correct action for a moving target&#x27;s old position and misses when it acts. Both response speed and observation freshness matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20665">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20665-torsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-814a0e85a5594988">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:torsi" data-paper-title="The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1cb9b40763fb601f">Why shouldn&#x27;t response latency and action age be combined into one metric?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atorsi">The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Samsung Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Response latency ends when the model returns; action age also includes queuing and applying the action. A live environment keeps changing, so a fast response can still be obsolete when applied. A slow teacher may practice and refine guidance from feedback only between attempts, and independent validation decides whether to replace it. It cannot peek at future live-test states to correct actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The model decides to jump within one second, but the command is queued for another two seconds and the obstacle is already gone. The three-second action age explains the failure better than one-second response latency alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20665">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20665-torsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1cb9b40763fb601f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:torsi" data-paper-title="The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-02ca6afaa67ea658">How does slow-teacher online takeover differ from TORSI&#x27;s offline guidance between attempts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atorsi">The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Samsung Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Online takeover places the slow model in real-time control, where delay can make its decisions obsolete. TORSI has the slow teacher analyze feedback and practice between attempts; guidance is then frozen and the fast student executes independently. The teacher cannot revise from test data. Guidance is accepted only for strictly positive gains on independent validation, and replay practice is not live execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher can explain a failed tracking run offline. In the next live run, the student must choose actions quickly on its own rather than pausing the world for step-by-step answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20665">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20665-torsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-02ca6afaa67ea658">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:torsi" data-paper-title="The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2759040921440d2b">Does TORSI accept new guidance on a validation tie, and what was tested locally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atorsi">The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Samsung Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Complete pairs with identical task IDs must show a strictly positive mean gain, and feedback, validation, and test remain separate. Timestamps must be finite and ordered. The local tests cover timing and numeric selection contracts only, with no game engine, Jev, or teacher run. Fixture differences in action age are not improvements in game progress.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If old and new guidance earn the same validation score, do not replace the old one because the new explanation is longer. Nor can you select it retroactively because its test score was slightly higher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20665">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20665-torsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2759040921440d2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harmony-harness" data-paper-title="Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harmony-harness-9020f112" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e5785ba0eb74fff6">Why not combine functionality and safety into an unconstrained average first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharmony-harness">Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Better functionality might come from relaxed checks, and an average can let a high functionality score offset serious safety regression. Harmony keeps both objectives and searches through preference subproblems and neighborhood replacement so deployments account for each. It is not a proof of safety against all attacks, and separate marginal rates are not joint success on the same trajectory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A trajectory can finish the task while leaking protected data. Mark functional success and safety failure rather than averaging it into a passing result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15150v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.15150-harmony-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e5785ba0eb74fff6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harmony-harness" data-paper-title="Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4036ffbcca6c9c03">Why isn&#x27;t min(functional success rate, safety success rate) the joint success rate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharmony-harness">Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The two marginal rates can come from different trajectories. Joint success requires both criteria to be met in the same execution. Multiobjective search uses preferences and neighborhood replacement to maintain trade-offs rather than increasing functional scores by weakening safety. Final selection and held-out reporting sets also need to remain separate, or reporting environments become search feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>In ten executions, eight can be functionally successful and eight safe while their failures do not overlap. Joint success can then be only six, so taking the minimum marginal count of eight overstates it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15150v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.15150-harmony-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4036ffbcca6c9c03">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harmony-harness" data-paper-title="Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-80c7d1bd28aa88ae">How does weighted Chebyshev differ from fixed linear weighting when retaining candidates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharmony-harness">Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Chebyshev uses the largest weighted deviation from the ideal point, emphasizing the weakest objective. Different preference vectors maintain separate harnesses; replacements require strict improvement in the neighborhood, with at most two per step. A fixed linear sum can let a large gain on one objective offset losses on another. The selection geometries differ, but both depend on reliable evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For a candidate with 90% functional success and 30% safety, maximum deviation highlights the safety weakness, whereas a simple average may still beat a more balanced option.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15150v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.15150-harmony-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-80c7d1bd28aa88ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harmony-harness" data-paper-title="Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4f53be87255685f">Can the final max-min selection choose the best harness on held-out OOD tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharmony-harness">Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Select the final harness by max-min over functionality and safety estimates from the search set, leaving held-out ID and OOD for evaluation. Joint success requires both criteria on the same trajectory. Locally there is no MOEA/D, real Docker environment, or exploit evaluation; a scalarization formula does not validate complete self-evolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the marginal rates are 80% functional and 70% safe, joint success is not necessarily 70%. Failures may occur on different tasks, so intersect successes trajectory by trajectory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与成本判断. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15150v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.15150-harmony-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4f53be87255685f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsi-anything" data-paper-title="RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-rsi-anything-7f27ef73" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-530166fda0dc63e5">Why does a world model&#x27;s prediction still need external validation feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-anything">RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · PhAI Labs / The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A prediction can screen consequences in advance but can be wrong; external tools or the environment supply actual evidence. RSI-Anything uses feedback to update persistent policy or workflow and updates the predictor only if reliability is insufficient and adaptation data and budget are adequate. A high predicted score is not verified task success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A programmatic layout predicted to be valid still needs a trusted geometry checker. If the result conflicts, record the prediction error instead of using the prediction as verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13912">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13912-rsi-anything/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-530166fda0dc63e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsi-anything" data-paper-title="RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7477ecc5f73f2292">Why check policy–predictor pair compatibility after each component passes its own checks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-anything">RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · PhAI Labs / The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The policy may depend on the old predictor&#x27;s state or assumptions. A new predictor can be accurate in isolation but incompatible with it. Test the behavior of both together and revert to the known pair if it fails. Predictor adaptation also requires insufficient reliability and enough data and budget. Automatic retraining each round or isolated component passes do not establish system improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a predictor changes the action encoding order and the policy still expects the old order, both unit tests may pass while integration fails. Roll back the combination rather than just recording two passes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13912">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13912-rsi-anything/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7477ecc5f73f2292">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsi-anything" data-paper-title="RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-38c1c449ff5f70c3">What is the trade-off between updating only the policy and adapting the world model too?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-anything">RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · PhAI Labs / The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed predictor gives a stable evaluator but may mislead persistently. Adaptation can address distribution shift, yet costs more and can alter interfaces the policy depends on. The framework gates adaptation by reliability, data, and budget and runs component and paired checks. Lower predictor loss does not by itself establish a better overall policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The old workflow may read the wrong field once the predictor learns a new feedback format. Check the pair rather than just verifying that both components can run in isolation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13912">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13912-rsi-anything/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-38c1c449ff5f70c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsi-anything" data-paper-title="RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a9314caa9163bb27">When may the predictor adapt, and why not update it after every failure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-anything">RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · PhAI Labs / The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Adaptation is triggered only when world-model reliability is insufficient, adaptation data are sufficient, and the remaining update budget covers the estimated cost. Failures do not necessarily come from the predictor, and updating on too few samples can chase noise. External verification does not remove the need for version attribution and pair compatibility checks. A short local run does not establish long-term self-improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A single erroneous prediction suggests unreliability, but without enough adaptation data or remaining budget, do not force training and call the resulting noisy update learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 结果、验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13912">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13912-rsi-anything/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a9314caa9163bb27">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness2" data-paper-title="Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harness2-5c8a24eb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-56f8f0526251b9f6">Why does Harness² study improving agent workflows without reference answers or scoring rubrics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness2">Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Many real tasks specify a deliverable without providing a callable correctness oracle. Execution probes can still expose workflow weaknesses. Harness² studies constructing a better harness through proposal, probing, and composition. Observed changes or high self-ratings do not show that an answer is correct; final artifacts need selection and checks separate from generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An open-ended research report has no unique answer. Probe source collection and organization and then inspect anonymized artifacts rather than trusting the author&#x27;s self-assessment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14224">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.14224-harness2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56f8f0526251b9f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness2" data-paper-title="Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cde1fd9a6db3a6fc">Without answers or rubrics, how does Propose–Probe–Compose avoid treating self-scores as a correctness oracle?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness2">Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidates are actually executed before composing them using public tasks and behavioral differences. Evidence comes from traces and artifacts rather than hidden answers. Anonymize artifacts during selection to reduce preference based on harness identity. This open-ended improvement procedure does not guarantee correctness; selector, reflection, and probe calls must count toward cost, not just final executions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A general proposal may strengthen verification and a domain proposal may improve retrieval. Combine useful parts after running them rather than assuming that a self-declared winner completed the task correctly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14224">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.14224-harness2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cde1fd9a6db3a6fc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness2" data-paper-title="Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b95ea9904b497c3">Why do parallel independent compositions and sequential recursive improvements have different candidate dependencies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness2">Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The parallel mode proposes general and domain candidates separately, then forms independent composites. Each sequential step reads the preceding harness and the within-task history, so it depends on earlier results. Both use 4k executions and 3k proposals; selectors and reflection are counted separately. Less waiting from parallelism does not reduce call cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With k=2, parallel execution yields two independent final composites, whereas the second sequential attempt builds on the first. Candidate dependencies are therefore different.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14224">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.14224-harness2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b95ea9904b497c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness2" data-paper-title="Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f178bdac3b099db">Why can the final selector only inspect anonymized artifacts, rather than harness identities or rewriting answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness2">Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Anonymity reduces preference based on proposal origin. The selector can only choose from final artifacts actually executed, without reference answers, proposal intermediates, or newly generated answers. At k=1, take the sole result directly. Trusted local scripted probes verify the execution accounting, not open-ended LLM performance, and outer arithmetic checks cannot feed back into the editor or reflector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the selector knows which output came from an &#x27;advanced&#x27; plan, it might favor that identity. If it edits the answer, it is no longer choosing from completed artifacts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14224">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.14224-harness2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8f178bdac3b099db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memento3" data-paper-title="Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-memento3-dd7ada6c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad1d7f6482680c52">Why does Memento 3 learn environmental rules for planning from black-box interaction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemento3">Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University College London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A new environment may not publish its transition rules. An agent sees actions and outcomes and can repeatedly err by guessing plans in language alone. Memento 3 organizes observations into a rulebook, compiles it into an executable model, and checks it with history and new actions so planning can occur in the model first. Learned rules are revisable hypotheses; agreement with history does not guarantee correctness in unseen states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a button changes an object&#x27;s orientation, propose a rotation rule and check other observed transitions. Revise the rule when new observations contradict it rather than ignoring the counterexample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11794">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.11794-memento3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad1d7f6482680c52">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memento3" data-paper-title="Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-81dc7395c90b6e8d">Why must historical replay avoid resetting simulated state from the next real observation at every step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemento3">Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University College London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Per-step resets hide accumulation of world-model errors and can make an incorrect model appear to match history. Continuous replay initializes from the first observation only, then generates subsequent states solely through model transitions, testing whether the rulebook really explains the trajectory. Semantic fidelity is checked separately; fitting finite history does not show general correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the first transition predicts the wrong door position, feeding the real screenshot at the second step erases the error. Continuous replay exposes its downstream consequences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11794">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.11794-memento3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-81dc7395c90b6e8d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memento3" data-paper-title="Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c135d3f3afc9d094">How does uniform sampling over complete-plan equivalence classes differ from voting by model member?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemento3">Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University College London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Several models may propose exactly the same action sequence. Sampling by member gives duplicates more probability. Group nonempty complete sequences and sample their classes uniformly to emphasize behavioral diversity rather than model counts. Follow the selected plan until completion, mismatch, or replanning; do not randomly switch paths at every step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If three models propose left-left and one proposes right-up, member sampling has 3:1 odds, while the two plan classes each get one-half probability. Duplicates do not amplify a route.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11794">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.11794-memento3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c135d3f3afc9d094">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memento3" data-paper-title="Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-66d5b7038bccdd48">Why must new world-model code pass both semantic fidelity and historical execution checks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemento3">Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University College London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Code might fit some observations without expressing the current rulebook, or faithfully implement an incorrect rule. The semantic check verifies that the compiled model matches the rules; historical replay checks that it recreates observed transitions. They constrain representation and behavior separately. Mismatches on new actions still trigger repairs, and a GPU execution receipt does not establish general rule correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rulebook specifies clockwise rotation, but the code hardcodes an output image. Passing one example by chance is not a faithful implementation of the rule.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11794">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.11794-memento3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-66d5b7038bccdd48">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mass" data-paper-title="Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-mass-a7f2d6e4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a53cbfd37dcfcacc">Why collect trajectories separately for frozen-weight search and subsequent SFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amass">Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Search for workflows first without confounding exploration with parameter changes. Then generate and rank fresh trajectories, train on better samples, reserve one for validation, and only then update the shared model. The same model executes, proposes, and evaluates, but that does not make self-scoring unbiased. Self-generated validation loss is not independent task accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A promising workflow during search still needs separately collected execution trajectories for training. An accidental high score from the same search trace is not independent validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12176">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12176-mass/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a53cbfd37dcfcacc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mass" data-paper-title="Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f2ba8ed1f9334346">Why remove the orchestrator&#x27;s initial workflow prompt before training but retain worker role assignments?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amass">Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The initial prompt contains the searched workflow. Retaining it directly could teach the model to rely on an external instruction rather than internalize useful collaboration. Worker roles preserve the execution structure and supervision applies to assistant tokens. Bradley–Terry ranking filters trajectories but self-ranked outcomes do not establish independent task capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the search prompt specifies retrieval then verification, remove that initial prompt so the model learns from successful execution, but keep the actual retriever and verifier turns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12176">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12176-mass/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f2ba8ed1f9334346">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mass" data-paper-title="Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c73c85ee811935d7">How does holding out the Kth Bradley–Terry-ranked trajectory differ from using all top trajectories for SFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amass">Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>After frozen-weight search, MASS independently collects trajectories and builds a BT ranking from pairwise comparisons. The first K−1 train the model and the Kth is for validation. The holdout separates training and checking targets, but the validation signal still comes from the chosen evaluator, not independent real-task success. Search traces cannot double as both training and generalization evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use the top two of three ranked trajectories to train and the third to validate. If the third also contributes to gradients, the validation loss no longer measures a true holdout.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12176">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12176-mass/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c73c85ee811935d7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mass" data-paper-title="Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3b165fac154d365c">What do two actual local LoRA rounds and lower validation loss establish?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amass">Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They show the shared-checkpoint execution, proposal, ranking, and update chain ran, including real parameter training in a constrained two-worker text workflow. The data were self-generated trajectories, with one seed and few steps. There were no arbitrary workflow graphs or research-file tools, so lower loss does not establish stronger independent research capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Round two may imitate its own validation text more easily and lower loss without ever testing whether its conclusions on unseen research tasks are correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12176">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12176-mass/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3b165fac154d365c">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoalloc" data-paper-title="EvoAlloc: A Self-Evolving Resource Allocation Agent for Efficient Program Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-evoalloc-9a5390ec" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6fe37e2f64ef258e">Why is continuing or stopping after Partial more flexible than an immediate Full/Discard decision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoalloc">EvoAlloc: A Self-Evolving Resource Allocation Agent for Efficient Program Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · King Abdullah University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Partial evaluation offers cheaper initial evidence before paying full cost, avoiding exhaustive evaluation of clearly bad candidates and premature discarding of potential winners. The task needs a trustworthy Partial signal; do not invent a score for an environment that does not support one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A quick program constraint check followed by a lengthy performance evaluation can be useful, but Circle26&#x27;s current interface has no Partial, so the local path supports only Full or Discard.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12086-evoalloc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6fe37e2f64ef258e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoalloc" data-paper-title="EvoAlloc: A Self-Evolving Resource Allocation Agent for Efficient Program Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea25419573e292b0">Why should some discarded candidates still receive counterfactual evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoalloc">EvoAlloc: A Self-Evolving Resource Allocation Agent for Efficient Program Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · King Abdullah University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If only selected programs are evaluated, the allocation policy cannot see high-quality candidates it missed and may become overly confident in its own preferences. Random counterfactual checks reveal the risk of missing a new best, and shadow policies need shared evidence. Those Full calls consume budget; do not exclude exploration or warmup to make savings look larger.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A filter may discard an unfamiliar implementation that an occasional full evaluation reveals to be superior. That evidence corrects selective feedback that equates unfamiliarity with low quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12086-evoalloc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea25419573e292b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoalloc" data-paper-title="EvoAlloc: A Self-Evolving Resource Allocation Agent for Efficient Program Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-89728affaf2b375a">How does prioritizing missed new bests before cost differ from minimizing Full evaluations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoalloc">EvoAlloc: A Self-Evolving Resource Allocation Agent for Efficient Program Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · King Abdullah University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Saving evaluations alone can miss the actual best candidate. Lexicographic ranking first protects search quality, then saves Full and Partial evaluations when missed-new-best counts tie. Random counterfactual checks of discarded candidates mitigate selective feedback, and shadow policies share evidence. Do not evaluate an allocator on accepted candidates alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If A avoids ten evaluations but misses a new champion, while B pays for two more evaluations and retains the champion, A should not advance merely for being cheaper.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12086-evoalloc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-89728affaf2b375a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoalloc" data-paper-title="EvoAlloc: A Self-Evolving Resource Allocation Agent for Efficient Program Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad4d7c9071244a6f">Why charge warmup, the shadow union, and counterfactual Full evaluations to the budget, and what did the short GPU run not trigger?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoalloc">EvoAlloc: A Self-Evolving Resource Allocation Agent for Efficient Program Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · King Abdullah University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They actually consume resources and are not free administrative work. Shadow promotion also requires two observed disagreements. The best of four real local Full evaluations did not beat the initial program. Warmup was insufficient and no promotion occurred. Partial and the two-disagreement case were covered only by contract tests, not triggered in the real run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a shadow policy requests a Full evaluation of a program discarded by the primary policy, charge it even if it never changes the primary champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12086-evoalloc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad4d7c9071244a6f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sentry" data-paper-title="Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-sentry-acd21bdd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-495464cea2ff924e">Why does Sentry specifically address stalls, repeated actions, and formatting errors during agent execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asentry">Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long-horizon agents can fail not just from missing knowledge but from loops, repeated ineffective actions, or invalid calls. Sentry detects such faults during execution and uses prior experience to support recovery. Resuming locally is not the same as ultimately answering correctly; the real local control comparison had a negative result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If an agent repeats an ineffective search, detection can trigger related advice. Even if it starts reading new pages, the final answer still needs to be checked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.02994-sentry/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-495464cea2ff924e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sentry" data-paper-title="Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ae4b0a62a5f04d6">Why add recovery advice to the playbook only after it is verified by observable later progress?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asentry">Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Advice proposed after failure is a hypothesis; saving it immediately can poison the playbook with bad remedies. An external verifier checks whether subsequent behavior actually recovers without reading task rewards to supply answers to the actor. Experiences are retrieved by failure class. Format errors follow hard repair, keeping mechanical correction distinct from semantic recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If &#x27;refresh login&#x27; still leads to repeated errors, do not store it. Progress through subsequent steps provides evidence that can be reused for similar failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.02994-sentry/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ae4b0a62a5f04d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sentry" data-paper-title="Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f2eab53b675d142d">What are the information trade-offs between retrieving recovery advice by failure class and keeping all experience in context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asentry">Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Conditional retrieval supplies relevant categories and tags only after detecting a matching failure, reducing input during normal execution. Always-on advice requires no trigger but adds irrelevant suggestions more readily. Conditional intervention depends on detection and matching: missed failures lose help, and false positives can disrupt a working policy. Less context alone does not imply more success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a network timeout, retrieving connection recovery is more focused than carrying format and loop repair guides at each step. Misreading normal waiting as a timeout can still make the intervention harmful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.02994-sentry/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f2eab53b675d142d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sentry" data-paper-title="Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc327101cfc3f1ce">Why can&#x27;t the local three-seed HotpotQA result be presented as improvement or as 24 independent tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asentry">Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Three generation seeds repeat the same eight questions. The mean was below baseline, and the extra manager and verifier calls added cost: this is a negative result. Memory is frozen after construction, holdout questions do not retune the detector, and a holdout derived from official validation is not the official test. A positive difference in one seed cannot override the overall decline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Seed 43 answers one more question correctly, but the other two perform worse. Report all paired outcomes to show instability rather than advertising only the best run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心规则与原文结果, 本地复现, 复现边界与失败记录. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.02994-sentry/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc327101cfc3f1ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seer-forecasting" data-paper-title="SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-seer-forecasting-fb9c59fb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e21ec395e7e0fe8">Why does SEER consider available external events in addition to numerical time series?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseer-forecasting">SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prices and demand can respond to news or policy that historical numbers alone cannot explain. SEER retrieves relevant events and improves filtering and knowledge from prior forecasting experience while keeping predictor weights fixed. Extra text can introduce noise and look-ahead risk, so check what was actually available at forecast time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An already announced holiday schedule may explain a demand shift. A sales report published afterward cannot be given to an earlier forecast, however clearly it explains the outcome.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04109v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.04109-seer-forecasting/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e21ec395e7e0fe8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seer-forecasting" data-paper-title="SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
