<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d160d05f468f8ca">Why must reflection wait for forecast outcomes to mature, with memory and causal knowledge frozen during testing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseer-forecasting">SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Future ground truth is unavailable at forecast time. Using it early to update retrieval or filtering leaks outcomes; updating memory from test errors also turns reporting into training feedback. Keeping retrieval memory, screening memory, and knowledge separate helps localize faults, but verify event time and actual availability independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>In a forecast of next week&#x27;s sales, weekend news cannot be inserted into Monday&#x27;s inputs. Sales learned after the test cannot be used to rewrite retrieval for that same test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04109v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.04109-seer-forecasting/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d160d05f468f8ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seer-forecasting" data-paper-title="SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d45948e73d7437d">How does fixing the forecasting model while updating retrieval and screening experience differ from fine-tuning its weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseer-forecasting">SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The former changes how external evidence is expanded, filtered, and organized, leaving predictor weights fixed so context evolution can be studied. Fine-tuning changes the internal mapping. The two memories and knowledge play different roles; a handwritten causal rule or new query template does not automatically teach the numerical model new dynamics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieval memory can suggest checking holidays, and screening memory can exclude irrelevant news, without changing the time-series model&#x27;s parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04109v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.04109-seer-forecasting/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d45948e73d7437d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seer-forecasting" data-paper-title="SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-96a96332cee84000">How do event occurrence and information availability jointly limit what a forecaster can read?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseer-forecasting">SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An event may already have occurred while reports or database entries become public later. Forecast inputs must satisfy the target-time and information-availability boundaries. The date on a story is not enough; check whether its contents were obtainable at the time. Memory can be compressed when capacity is limited, but compression cannot inject future conclusions into past contexts, and test-time reflection is forbidden.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An event occurs Monday but is disclosed Wednesday. Tuesday&#x27;s forecast must not use Wednesday&#x27;s story, even if the headline is relabeled with Monday&#x27;s date.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与成本判断. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04109v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.04109-seer-forecasting/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96a96332cee84000">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:frugalevo" data-paper-title="FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-frugalevo-468f3ba3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-68885a6d3cab967b">Why does FrugalEvo want cheaper models to implement strong-model research ideas repeatedly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afrugalevo">FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Using a strong model for every generation and execution step is costly, while a weaker one may lack good strategies. FrugalEvo joins stronger strategy proposals with cheaper repeated implementation to find useful programs within a budget. Evaluate actual costs and quality over the whole search, not just the final best score or a cheap individual call.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A strong model suggests a direction and a weak model tries several code variants. If repeated failures still consume substantial budget, the division of labor may not pay off.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.03675-frugalevo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-68885a6d3cab967b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:frugalevo" data-paper-title="FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-08a5a44572618256">Why follow an expensive model&#x27;s strategy proposal with repeated cheap execution, and assess the full best-so-far curve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afrugalevo">FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Strategic planning and local code iteration require different capabilities and costs. Hierarchy reserves expensive calls for direction setting. Failures add feedback while retaining the parent program; improvement re-anchors search, and an island archive protects diversity. The best-so-far curve over the budget reflects how early useful solutions emerge, not just a lucky final score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A strong model proposes vectorization and a smaller model tests several equivalent implementations. Finding a useful speedup earlier under the same budget is more informative than one chance best at the end.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.03675-frugalevo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-08a5a44572618256">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:frugalevo" data-paper-title="FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b570190e7adc039e">How should a costly strategy model plus cheap implementer be fairly compared with weak-model-only search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afrugalevo">FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Start both from the same program, budget, and call caps, but actual costs can differ when different limits bind first. Larger models are not necessarily stronger; report actual tokens, strategy trials, and refinement. The architecture does not imply collaboration always wins, and overall local results did not support that conclusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the weak model hits its 30-call cap with budget left and the collaboration consumes more tokens, report &#x27;same caps,&#x27; not &#x27;same actual cost.&#x27;</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.03675-frugalevo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b570190e7adc039e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:frugalevo" data-paper-title="FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1f4b7fda8831b85">Why retain the parent after a generated program fails and reject fallback to bare exec?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afrugalevo">FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use failure feedback for the next revision without replacing a verified parent with invalid code. Actual generated code requires Linux isolation and resource limits; fail closed if the sandbox does not start. Do not trust model-reported scores: a trusted checker verifies bounds and non-overlap. Do not dress up a negative local result by deleting failed calls or relaxing security boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An invalid radius counts as a failed proposal and costs a call. Do not substitute the parent&#x27;s answer and mark the candidate successful, or run it on the host when the sandbox is unavailable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 公式与原文结果, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.03675-frugalevo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1f4b7fda8831b85">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:flowright" data-paper-title="It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-flowright-b0c3085e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-769d988dd4262bbd">Why is it hard to decide which role to improve if a multi-agent workflow gets only a terminal result?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aflowright">It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · William &amp; Mary</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success depends jointly on roles and dependencies. Giving everyone the same reward hides who moved the workflow forward or held it back. FlowRight organizes role credit using workflow structure to support improvements at different scopes. Structural weights are an attribution rule, not direct measurements of each role&#x27;s causal contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A retriever finds good evidence but a writer misreads it. Identical failure scores could lead subsequent updates to damage a useful retrieval habit as well.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01026-flowright/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-769d988dd4262bbd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:flowright" data-paper-title="It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bff8ef395659ef30">Why does topology-aware role credit use workflow structure instead of averaging terminal reward across all roles?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aflowright">It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · William &amp; Mary</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Roles occupy different positions and affect different downstream steps. Equal credit can conceal a bad node or a critical upstream role. Topological weights incorporate validity and successors, supporting both single-role changes and upstream/downstream collaboration in one framework. This is an attribution rule, not identification of causal contributions; use execution comparisons to test it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a retriever&#x27;s error reaches three downstream roles, repairing it may matter more than polishing the final paragraph. The topology shows the propagation range instead of dividing reward by headcount.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01026-flowright/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bff8ef395659ef30">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:flowright" data-paper-title="It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e685b943960b7cf">Which participants change in single-role evolution, upstream–downstream collaboration, and joint multi-role evolution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aflowright">It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · William &amp; Mary</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single-role update fixes the other participants to isolate a local change. Upstream–downstream collaboration targets the dependency interface. Joint changes can improve coordination across roles, but their effects are harder to attribute. FlowRight expresses those scopes with a common workflow and credit representation. Success at one scope does not guarantee every joint update works.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing just the writer and changing both retriever and writer may require different validation. The pair may adapt to a new evidence format, so gains cannot be attributed entirely to writing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01026-flowright/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e685b943960b7cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:flowright" data-paper-title="It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5eae1a0fd5db0e8">What should an implementation of valid_i(1+children_i) check, and what was not completed locally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aflowright">It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · William &amp; Mary</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Invalid roles get zero weight. Normalize over all valid weights, verify conservation of credit, and handle the no-valid-item case. The local path only executes this allocation operator; it does not generate workflows, train Qwen3.5, or run DataWright. Passing structural tests does not establish improvement from multi-agent co-evolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An invalid node with ten children should receive no credit. When all nodes are invalid, handle the case explicitly rather than dividing by zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01026-flowright/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5eae1a0fd5db0e8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:active-saddler" data-paper-title="ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-active-saddler-9c3dd285" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb7aff962dad76a3">With a limited repair budget, why does ActiveSaddler choose which failures to expose next?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aactive-saddler">ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A harness cannot repair all scenarios equally deeply at once, and repeatedly testing familiar problems misses new weaknesses. ActiveSaddler treats the training curriculum as a dynamic decision based on existing failures and repair feedback. Selecting a difficult scenario only creates a learning opportunity; it does not establish a repair, and scheduling counts are not real capability gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>File-editing failures have been fixed repeatedly, while browser recovery issues just appeared. The curriculum must choose whether to keep verifying old behavior or budget exploration for the new fault.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00906">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00906-active-saddler/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb7aff962dad76a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:active-saddler" data-paper-title="ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd6e14f5e934fc23">Why must failure modes treated as nonstationary bandit arms allow discovery of new scenarios and revisiting old weaknesses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aactive-saddler">ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A harness repair changes the payoff of previous failures. A fixed curriculum may keep testing solved problems while missing newly exposed faults. The controller allocates budget using value and exploration terms, periodically introducing unseen scenarios to support both discovery and verification. Counts or priorities are curriculum signals, not model capability metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After fixing timeouts, practice them less often but occasionally retest for regressions while exploring previously uncovered permission errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00906">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00906-active-saddler/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd6e14f5e934fc23">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:active-saddler" data-paper-title="ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4c5ad7e44c1c3e3">Do fixed hard-task sampling and dynamically reprioritizing failures after repairs face the same stationary rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aactive-saddler">ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed sampling generally follows preset difficulty or frequencies. Repairs change the value of prior failures: formerly frequent problems may no longer deserve repeated investment, while new ones appear. Dynamic scheduling should update with this nonstationary feedback. Historical failure rates are not permanent estimates of current reward, and revisits may yield no new information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a parser fix, old hard examples consistently pass. Filling the curriculum with them wastes budget; newly observed authentication issues may deserve more attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00906">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00906-active-saddler/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4c5ad7e44c1c3e3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:active-saddler" data-paper-title="ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-49be3a394da7a5ca">Does the local dynamic arm scheduler run AutoSaddler&#x27;s real repair chain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aactive-saddler">ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It creates failure arms, explores and exploits, and updates priorities. It does not call AutoSaddler or run real GAIA2 or Terminal-Bench tasks. Observation counts and selection weights verify scheduling, not harness repair from synthetic feedback. Account for real rollout costs separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If lowering an arm&#x27;s synthetic reward reduces its selections, the controller responds to changes. It does not show that any actual tool failure was resolved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00906">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00906-active-saddler/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-49be3a394da7a5ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rule-evolve" data-paper-title="Self-Evolving Coding Rules for AI Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-rule-evolve-f1ced1e2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-846804b9a08fcd6a">Why does RuleEvolve treat coding rules as development experience that can be tested and revised?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arule-evolve">Self-Evolving Coding Rules for AI Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Coding-agent rules affect recurring search, editing, and testing behavior, and one manually written tip might not fit the task distribution. RuleEvolve selects variants with behavioral evidence so experience can be revised. More detailed wording is not better execution; use isolated validation rather than the generator&#x27;s confidence to update rules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After adding &#x27;check callers before editing,&#x27; test whether it helps repair the same development tasks, not just whether it sounds sensible.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00650">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00650-rule-evolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-846804b9a08fcd6a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rule-evolve" data-paper-title="Self-Evolving Coding Rules for AI Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4060e8043015f09">Why can&#x27;t a mutator write back a coding rule based only on its own assessment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arule-evolve">Self-Evolving Coding Rules for AI Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A plausible rule may fit only a few examples or damage old behavior. An isolated validation evaluator measures the candidate pool and variants consistently and selects what to write back, separating proposals from acceptance evidence. Selection data are development feedback; do not expose final tests to repeated mutator tuning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new rule that retries every function sounds robust but can repeat non-idempotent operations. Independent validation can reveal this regression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00650">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00650-rule-evolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4060e8043015f09">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rule-evolve" data-paper-title="Self-Evolving Coding Rules for AI Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c0648898c9a12dc">How does retaining a rule candidate pool differ from immediately overwriting the only rule, for search and rollback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arule-evolve">Self-Evolving Coding Rules for AI Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A pool compares multiple versions under one evaluation protocol and retains old rules as baselines or candidates. Immediate overwrite makes the proposal active and can lose a usable baseline after failure. A pool does not supply a correct judge by itself; it still needs an isolated evaluator. Candidate counts are not actual performance on tool tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep both a retrieval-focused rule and a testing-focused rule for comparison. If each generation immediately overwrites the rule, it is hard to tell which change caused a regression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00650">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00650-rule-evolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c0648898c9a12dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rule-evolve" data-paper-title="Self-Evolving Coding Rules for AI Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0dd59670d06cd928">Does local selection after mutation establish that LLM rule evolution ran?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arule-evolve">Self-Evolving Coding Rules for AI Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It checks validation selection among mutated candidates but does not call an LLM mutator or full coding agent. Correct argmax over supplied scores is control-flow evidence; if scores come from fixtures, they do not indicate code quality. Retain old rules and failed candidates for audit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choosing the largest of three preset scores verifies the selector. Without a model proposing rules and actually fixing code, it does not verify the whole self-evolution path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00650">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00650-rule-evolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0dd59670d06cd928">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:video-rsi" data-paper-title="Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-video-rsi-6a868dfd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-852af1294a326d1e">Why might a video agent need to improve evidence collection rather than just use a stronger answer prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avideo-rsi">Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long video spans many moments and details. The failure may occur during frame selection, localization, reading, or organizing evidence, rather than composing the final answer. Video RSI uses execution to improve the video-task harness so limited cost is spent on relevant evidence. A changed workflow alone is not better understanding; check both accuracy and actual cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the question asks what someone did before leaving and the agent samples only the start and end, rewording the final prompt will not reveal the key middle action. Improve evidence gathering first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37950">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.37950-video-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-852af1294a326d1e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:video-rsi" data-paper-title="Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a4bdd987fbb14e7">Why can reading only a failed trace be insufficient to diagnose evidence collection in a video agent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avideo-rsi">Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A trace records only what the old harness chose to observe; unseen keyframes cannot be recovered from that log. Revisit training video to gather observations and test whether evidence was omitted or reasoning was wrong, then change the interface. Acceptance retains accuracy and cost gates so a weighted total cannot hide a clear regression in either.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the old policy sampled only the opening while the key action came at the end, the trace omits it. Revisiting the original training video verifies that sampling rather than wording needs to change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37950">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.37950-video-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a4bdd987fbb14e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:video-rsi" data-paper-title="Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b4df352f6dc0c05f">What do dual accuracy and cost gates protect compared with a single weighted score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avideo-rsi">Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A candidate must not lower accuracy or increase cost, and at least one measure must strictly improve. This prevents large gains on one objective from hiding deterioration on the other. Declare tolerances before selection rather than relaxing them to accept a candidate. Dual gates still require the same measurement protocol and do not guarantee generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A candidate that loses ten accuracy points while halving frame count could win a weighted sum but violates the no-regression requirement and should be rejected.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37950">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.37950-video-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b4df352f6dc0c05f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:video-rsi" data-paper-title="Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c1480a393a3ca8e">Why isn&#x27;t a passing local Pareto gate registered as an executable Evolve operator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avideo-rsi">Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>There is no real video decoding, code-rewriting sandbox, or cross-generation stopping condition, so the controller cannot fully execute and evaluate a candidate. The gate only checks acceptance relations over supplied metrics. Fixture scores do not establish video-agent improvement, and a registry name or three-seed rule check is not end-to-end evolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two sets of numbers suffice to calculate dominance, but without obtaining them by running a candidate harness on video there is no capability evidence for promotion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37950">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.37950-video-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c1480a393a3ca8e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-skills" data-paper-title="Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-meta-skills-2db3e168" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e92a721ec01e3781">Why does Meta-Skills focus on transferable experience about configuring how an agent works?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-skills">Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apodex / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar tasks can share planning, evidence collection, or verification routines. Keeping only individual answers forces the next task to redesign the workflow. Meta-Skills makes procedural experience reusable through retrieval that guides the harness. Experience needs applicability conditions; a prompt that helped one question should not be applied everywhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Building an evidence table before comparing numbers across sources is procedural knowledge. The actual numbers belong to the original task and should not be reused as new answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38143">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.38143-meta-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e92a721ec01e3781">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-skills" data-paper-title="Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a366ef3d536dcd6">Why specify when, provide, and use in a meta-skill rather than just &#x27;verify more in future&#x27;?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-skills">Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apodex / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>When gives the trigger, provide specifies the resource, and use describes integration. Together they turn generic advice into retrievable design knowledge. Freeze the library after development and retrieve only to construct the harness in testing. If test results revise the library, the test no longer measures transfer of fixed skills to unseen tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>&#x27;When tool output is incomplete, provide access to raw logs and inspect them before retrying&#x27; can become a concrete runtime component more readily than &#x27;be more careful.&#x27;</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38143">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.38143-meta-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a366ef3d536dcd6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-skills" data-paper-title="Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-07f0a4ee787f4c47">How does frozen-library retrieval during testing differ from writing experience back while testing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-skills">Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apodex / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freezing tests transfer from development. Writing back from test feedback lets later tasks exploit evaluation results and changes the test information contract. Allowed observations in the current task can inform its harness, but private test scores cannot revise the long-term library or reselect reported results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding a rule tailored to a failed test1 and rerunning test1 is not frozen-library generalization. Report it under a separate learning protocol.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38143">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.38143-meta-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-07f0a4ee787f4c47">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-skills" data-paper-title="Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e690a5adb56993a1">How do local development refinement and frozen retrieval limit the conclusions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-skills">Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apodex / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local checks verify that the library accepts development feedback, freezes against write-back during retrieval, and maintains related state invariants. Fixture rewards are not the AI4AI benchmark. Without a real harness proposer and task model, matching a when field neither establishes generalizable design learning nor reproduces reported paper gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Finding a meta-skill tagged &#x27;long text&#x27; tests routing. It does not test whether the skill improves real long-context tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38143">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.38143-meta-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e690a5adb56993a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:branch-mixture" data-paper-title="Mixture of Self-Improving Branches for Agent Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-branch-mixture-203f2124" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d71231e390a01996">Why should branches maintain different development subsets and proposal policies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abranch-mixture">Mixture of Self-Improving Branches for Agent Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>When all branches see the same examples and use the same proposals, they can converge to redundant harnesses. Distinct subsets and strategies preserve specialization that the router can select by input. Additional branches also increase development cost; do not hide total search budget when comparing with one branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One branch can specialize in tool formats and another in long-horizon verification, giving routing meaningful alternatives rather than copies under different names.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.37834-branch-mixture/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d71231e390a01996">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:branch-mixture" data-paper-title="Mixture of Self-Improving Branches for Agent Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-aabf9fb0b40ae634">Why remove development examples solved by every branch while retaining examples that distinguish branches?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abranch-mixture">Mixture of Self-Improving Branches for Agent Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared solved examples provide little information about branch differences and can dilute weaknesses while consuming budget. Each branch retains a discriminating subset and proposal strategy, and a deployment router picks a development champion by input. An adaptive development set is not an independent final test; routing cannot use test labels to choose a winner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If all branches solve simple sorting but graph search distinguishes two strategies, devote more curriculum budget to the latter rather than repeatedly testing common strengths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.37834-branch-mixture/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aabf9fb0b40ae634">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:branch-mixture" data-paper-title="Mixture of Self-Improving Branches for Agent Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a69ceef4c84d93f">What assumption differs between routing across specialist branches and always running one global champion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abranch-mixture">Mixture of Self-Improving Branches for Agent Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A global champion assumes one harness covers all inputs. Branch mixtures allow workflows to specialize and choose among them from public input features. Specialization may improve fit but adds routing errors and maintenance cost. Routing must use deployment-visible information, not current test gold scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Code and browsing tasks can have different development champions. Routing by task features is deployable; reading both branches&#x27; gold scores on the current test before choosing is not.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.37834-branch-mixture/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a69ceef4c84d93f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:branch-mixture" data-paper-title="Mixture of Self-Improving Branches for Agent Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6112ff8a7f4f4deb">May a deployment router read branches&#x27; true scores on the current test item to pick the winner?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abranch-mixture">Mixture of Self-Improving Branches for Agent Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use input features to select a development champion without test labels or future execution scores. The local implementation provides subset diversification and linear routing, not LLM-generated harnesses or SWE-bench runs. Correct branch choice on fixtures does not show real mixture gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Running all branches and selecting the hidden judge&#x27;s best result is an oracle ensemble, not deployment routing based on request inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.37834-branch-mixture/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6112ff8a7f4f4deb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-learning" data-paper-title="Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harness-learning-a67122de" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad3546d8176fcc6f">Why does Harness Learning treat tool protocols, memory, and planning as learnable objects?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-learning">Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>With the same weights, the external workflow still controls what the model sees, when it calls tools, and how it recovers. Harness Learning uses feedback to revise executable organization rather than attributing every weakness to the base model. Workflow adaptation is a distinct scope and does not imply new capability learned in model parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Add testing before every submission without changing the base model. Outcomes may change because execution was organized differently, not because weights were trained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.35738-harness-learning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad3546d8176fcc6f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-learning" data-paper-title="Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6385fbc64265b44">How can test-time adaptation occur with frozen task-model weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-learning">Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Adaptation changes executable components outside the model, such as verification, interpreters, retrieval, and retry protocols. Execution feedback changes that scaffolding and therefore later behavior of the same model. This is not fine-tuning and cannot route hidden answers through the interface to a proposer. Local classification-policy updates are not the paper&#x27;s full LLM adaptation chain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep the model fixed, but add shell-output truncation and error localization after a failure. The next attempt can process the output better without any neural-weight change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.35738-harness-learning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6385fbc64265b44">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-learning" data-paper-title="Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fdbd2dc11b469064">How does within-group relative-reward training of the revision policy differ from fixed hand-written rules?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-learning">Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Locally, subtract the group&#x27;s mean execution score from each candidate score to form advantages and apply REINFORCE to revision logits. Feedback can change proposal preferences; fixed rules learn no parameters. The small classification proposer is not the paper&#x27;s general harness learner, and a formula alone does not establish safe arbitrary component changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A revision that performs better within its group gets positive advantage and becomes more likely, instead of being predetermined by a rule author.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.35738-harness-learning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fdbd2dc11b469064">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-learning" data-paper-title="Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6af322ce5a688d5e">Why do external callbacks not establish integration with a general agent runner or Evolve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-learning">Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A trusted callback is an execution interface. A general system must safely run arbitrary harnesses and isolate validation. That full chain is missing. Adaptation inputs allow only scores and failure categories, not gold data or hidden verifier fields. Mini-suite success is not open-ended agent capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A callback that returns a preset high score can test loop control, but without real candidate execution it supplies no promotion evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.35738-harness-learning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6af322ce5a688d5e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentx-model-replay" data-paper-title="Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agentx-model-replay-82b929d4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-026d2b5abf0f0211">Why does AgentX-Model need to connect each research choice to actual experiments?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx-model-replay">Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Automated research must choose what to try and obtain new evidence through implementation and evaluation, not just generate proposals. Research and model execution roles exchange proposals so search history reflects attempted candidates. Historical replay only reenacts revelation and selection of existing outcomes; it does not rerun training locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a proposal to change the loss, the implementer returns results only after training. A replay should likewise reveal a score only after selecting the candidate, without peeking at future outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.30001-agentx-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-026d2b5abf0f0211">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentx-model-replay" data-paper-title="Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-900b22adccd50c90">Why connect the Research Agent and Model Agent through proposals instead of sharing full experiment logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx-model-replay">Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Proposals specify the question, constraints, and approved direction. The model implementer runs iterative experiments under fixed business inputs and prediction tasks, preventing mutual context overload. Return interim bests, negative results, and unresolved questions for the next research decision. The interface carries evidence, not just one appealing final score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Researchers can propose a long-history compression hypothesis. The model agent reports the best version and when it fails, allowing the next hypothesis without showing every compilation log.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.30001-agentx-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-900b22adccd50c90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentx-model-replay" data-paper-title="Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-24e0589e2f1f44db">Why does improvement over a parent differ from setting a new best over the entire ancestral path?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx-model-replay">Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If a parent regressed, its child can recover some performance without beating an older champion. Track both the parent delta and comparable ancestral delta to avoid presenting recovery as a breakthrough. Diagnose actions primarily reduce uncertainty and should not be ranked by the same immediate AUC objective as improvement actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If an ancestor has AUC .80, parent .75, and child .78, the child gains .03 over its parent but is still .02 below the path best. Report both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.30001-agentx-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24e0589e2f1f44db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentx-model-replay" data-paper-title="Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e537d66be10432b">When are candidate outcomes revealed in historical replay, and how does local data avoid future leakage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx-model-replay">Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A child can be selected only after its parent, and the candidate&#x27;s result is revealed only after selection. MovieLens holds out the last two chronological interactions for validation and test; training statistics cannot read future events, and champions use validation only. A rule-based selector and logistic-regression replay are not the paper&#x27;s LLM research agent or an online A/B replication.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Even if the logs contain a high score from another branch, the selector cannot read it before deciding to try that branch. Otherwise it has a future-metric oracle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 可执行路径与防泄漏边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.30001-agentx-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e537d66be10432b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
