<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sciencebuddy" data-paper-title="ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-sciencebuddy-cd9b47fe" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3463aea1843b4ca">Why does ScienceBuddy put tool interaction and policy learning into one continuing process for scientific tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asciencebuddy">ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gen-Verse research collaboration</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scientific tasks involve proposing actions, using tools, interpreting observations, and adjusting plans. A fixed prompt is unlikely to handle ongoing feedback. ScienceBuddy studies improving workflows and policies together during interaction. Track the two levels separately; simulated state updates are not evidence of a real scientific environment or model training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A search finds the original hypothesis lacks evidence, so the workflow can require source checks first. Whether the policy learned that judgment needs validation on subsequent real tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17523-sciencebuddy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3463aea1843b4ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sciencebuddy" data-paper-title="ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-83f78a9174f9ee29">Why can&#x27;t inner harness evolution and outer policy updates be reduced to repeatedly rewriting a prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asciencebuddy">ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gen-Verse research collaboration</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The two levels change different objects. The inner loop optimizes interaction, while the outer loop uses successful trajectories to update the scientific agent&#x27;s parameterized policy, which affects the next inner search. Actual execution, filtering, and training must close the loop to demonstrate recursion within recursion. Reference gates or synthetic statistics cannot replace the models and environments involved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Find a better experimental checking process, then train the agent on successful trajectories so it uses that process better next time. Rewriting the prompt three times has no second-layer update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17523-sciencebuddy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-83f78a9174f9ee29">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sciencebuddy" data-paper-title="ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec29bbe804bbe212">What trade-offs arise from two-level feedback versus single-level training with a fixed harness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asciencebuddy">ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gen-Verse research collaboration</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Two levels can improve both data generation and policy, but simultaneous changes complicate attribution and introduce nonstationarity. Record versions, trajectory provenance, and updates separately. A fixed harness is easier to control but can constrain exploration. Mechanism comparisons do not replace scientific-task or experimental outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A higher outer-loop score might come from better tool feedback or from new parameters. Without versions, the contributions are hard to distinguish.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17523-sciencebuddy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec29bbe804bbe212">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sciencebuddy" data-paper-title="ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-04bf786ad243175c">Does the local double-state reference include a lab and real scientific policy learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asciencebuddy">ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gen-Verse research collaboration</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It runs a reference two-level state update and gate, without a real laboratory, full scientific tasks, or paper-scale training. Three-seed intermediate values verify branches and information flow, not reproducible scientific discovery rates. Counts of state updates do not validate full recursive learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two inner changes and one outer update show control-state movement. Without real trajectories and gradients, they do not show that the policy learned a task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17523-sciencebuddy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-04bf786ad243175c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:maple" data-paper-title="MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-maple-2e42a8d7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf5ce6d0765f08ca">Why does MAPLE aim to retain optimization knowledge across consecutive solves?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amaple">MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Related tasks often share structure. Starting each proposal from scratch makes verified program improvements hard to accumulate. MAPLE uses executable solutions as persistent research state and explores subsequent problems from accepted programs. Inheritance can carry stale assumptions, so verify the new constraints rather than treating executability or historical success as proof of current optimality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reuse a scheduling program that already resolves resource conflicts, but implement and test the new time-window constraint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11636-maple/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf5ce6d0765f08ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:maple" data-paper-title="MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fedfb0ce31b03cfb">Why can starting subsequent problems from an accepted program accumulate optimization knowledge better than reprompting from scratch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amaple">MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Program state preserves verified executable structure and trade-offs. The next task can modify it rather than reconstruct details from language. Acceptance prevents unexecuted ideas from overwriting a reliable parent. Cross-problem evolution still needs to account for task differences: a specialized program for one instance is not universally best.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the previous problem already has reliable parsing, change its objective for the next task rather than regenerate a blank script and repeat format mistakes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11636-maple/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fedfb0ce31b03cfb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:maple" data-paper-title="MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8144cd5a6a2e654d">How does accepting an executable program differ from accepting an optimization description that sounds better?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amaple">MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A description conveys intent. A program must run and pass the relevant comparison before becoming evolvable state. Executability does not imply improvement: validity and benefit are separate gates. A one-time gain does not generalize to all future tasks, and failed proposals should not be inherited unconditionally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>&#x27;Reduce redundant search&#x27; is advice. Accept the optimization only after it changes the call logic and verifies that required evidence was not missed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11636-maple/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8144cd5a6a2e654d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:maple" data-paper-title="MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-97e540f60a62b382">How does local validation of nonempty named-operation plans differ from the authors&#x27; solver?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amaple">MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The local path accepts public plans made of nonempty named operations and checks reuse. It has no author solver, trained model, or external tools. Structural execution contracts can be tested, but perfect mini-suite scores are not paper-level optimization or general program evolution. A missing solver cannot be substituted with a registry name.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Nodes named &#x27;search&#x27; and &#x27;verify&#x27; pass the nonempty structural check, but do not demonstrate that a real search algorithm outperforms its predecessor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11636-maple/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97e540f60a62b382">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ecdysis" data-paper-title="Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ecdysis-3d533dc6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a195b04da4575d0d">Why does Ecdysis ask whether failures are occasional model behavior or shared runtime defects?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aecdysis">Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chengdu Institute of Computer Applications, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Failures across tasks can be individual misunderstandings, or recurrent effects of tool wrapping, context, and recovery. Ecdysis looks across executions for repairable harness defects so changes target shared causes. Recurrence is a diagnostic clue, not a completed fix without execution and verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If several tasks lose evidence because tool output is truncated, suspect a common interface. A single task that misreads content does not justify immediately changing every workflow.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11677">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11677-ecdysis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a195b04da4575d0d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ecdysis" data-paper-title="Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bdf6583baffee7b9">Why aggregate similar failures across tasks to diagnose a systemic harness defect?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aecdysis">Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chengdu Institute of Computer Applications, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single failure may be due to randomness or a particular prompt. A recurring pattern more strongly suggests a shared execution interface problem. Multi-role diagnosis turns the evidence into a testable repair specification instead of changing global behavior after each failure. Correlation is not sufficient causal proof; compare affected behaviors after repair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many tasks losing error codes when logs are truncated gives stronger reason to inspect the output interface than one bad guess. Target truncation rather than generally replacing the model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11677">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11677-ecdysis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bdf6583baffee7b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ecdysis" data-paper-title="Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd6fec7b3d5c110c">Where do a repair specification and direct execution of a harness patch sit in the improvement chain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aecdysis">Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chengdu Institute of Computer Applications, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>FDCR&#x27;s multi-role diagnosis organizes failure evidence into a discussable repair specification describing what to change and why. Execution still requires a concrete patch, runtime integration, and verification. A diagnosis is not a changed system; gate triggers or counts of repair suggestions do not indicate task-success gains. This boundary is especially important for the local reference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A specification says &#x27;preserve tool error fields.&#x27; Check the patch and execution logs separately to see whether the code actually changed and worked in later tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11677">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11677-ecdysis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd6fec7b3d5c110c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ecdysis" data-paper-title="Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb9a1324918e6565">Does triggering the local FDCR repair gate mean a harness patch was generated or executed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aecdysis">Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chengdu Institute of Computer Applications, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The local path aggregates signatures from public observations and triggers a bounded repair gate. It does not generate or execute code or run paper-scale training. A trigger shows the statistics satisfy a condition, not correct diagnosis or actual repair. Three-seed counts cannot be converted into paper speed or accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A &#x27;needs repair&#x27; state after three similar failures is a scheduling signal. Without a patch and rerun, the defect is not resolved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11677">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11677-ecdysis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb9a1324918e6565">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cobra-skills" data-paper-title="COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-cobra-skills-f91c343f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1c56fd2f44841929">Why can&#x27;t COBRA-Skills give each candidate the same number of trials as the skill pool grows?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acobra-skills">COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Evaluating skills consumes execution budget while the number and quality of candidates change. Equal allocation can waste trials on clearly useless or duplicate entries. COBRA-Skills combines current context with past feedback to direct limited trials. Selectors may only use available evidence, not presume effects of unexecuted candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten similar skills have repeatedly failed and a newly generated one may deserve limited exploration. Running every candidate a hundred times is not feasible on a tight budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11682">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11682-cobra-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1c56fd2f44841929">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cobra-skills" data-paper-title="COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f97cc70d3ab4160">Why use a budgeted contextual bandit for dynamic skill candidates rather than ranking historical best scores alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acobra-skills">COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Skill payoff depends on the current task, and new or revised candidates lack history. A contextual bandit balances exploiting known gains and exploring informative candidates under an evaluation budget, then evolves from execution feedback. Historical maxima can favor early lucky skills and ignore context and uncertainty about untested candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If an old skill excels at files but new tasks are web-based, giving new candidates a few trials may be more informative than repeatedly testing the old champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11682">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11682-cobra-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f97cc70d3ab4160">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cobra-skills" data-paper-title="COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd3c458ed7ccbf9b">Why separate proposing a skill variant from measuring its execution reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acobra-skills">COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A proposal uses existing experience to describe potentially better behavior but does not establish usefulness on this task. Only execution supplies feedback for budget allocation and evolution. The space may grow dynamically, but membership does not imply positive reward. COBRA-Skills bandit selection must distinguish measured payoff from uncertainty rather than fill missing results with proposal self-assessment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A more detailed skill can be scheduled for a trial. Only actual execution shows whether it helps; &#x27;expected improvement&#x27; is not a successful sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11682">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11682-cobra-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dd3c458ed7ccbf9b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cobra-skills" data-paper-title="COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e657576f6a249149">Does local contextual-UCB allocation cover actual LLM skill evolution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acobra-skills">COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It executes a reference allocator and feedback admission gate, with no external LLM or six environments. Candidate indices, confidence terms, and budget can be checked independently, but actual skill-text generation and task execution did not occur. Fixture feedback is not actual cost savings or capability gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Selecting a numeric arm after its UCB grows checks the bandit formula. It does not demonstrate that the corresponding natural-language skill works on web tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11682">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11682-cobra-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e657576f6a249149">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:procedural-graphs" data-paper-title="Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-procedural-graphs-6aeeaceb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0813fc391c0f0f1c">What does a procedure–relation–procedure graph add beyond storing skill snippets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprocedural-graphs">Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A graph explicitly represents dependencies and compositions, so new experience can change a local execution structure rather than add similar prose. Correct relations matter for downstream paths. Validate edits on an independent holdout before permanent write-back, not just because a trace succeeded once.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>&#x27;Query after authentication&#x27; is an ordering relation and &#x27;refresh credentials if the query fails&#x27; is recovery. Two separate text snippets might not express those links.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.09153-procedural-graphs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0813fc391c0f0f1c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:procedural-graphs" data-paper-title="Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-495c2876d5383645">Why localize experience as a graph edit before a held-out gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprocedural-graphs">Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Procedural relations affect multiple paths, and overwriting them with whole episodes can contaminate unrelated skills. Local edits identify the affected node or relation; held-out verification tests whether the change goes beyond incidental success in the originating trace. A pass supports only its evaluation scope, not global reliability inferred from coherent training traces.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Add only a recovery edge to refresh a token after authentication failure. Check independent tasks for redundant authentication rather than rewriting the whole upload graph.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.09153-procedural-graphs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-495c2876d5383645">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:procedural-graphs" data-paper-title="Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-36893bcf703a5f2a">What trade-offs arise from a local graph edit versus rewriting the entire procedure graph?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprocedural-graphs">Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local changes reduce unrelated effects and ease attribution and rollback. Whole-graph rewrites allow more freedom but can break old interfaces and valid paths. Locality does not guarantee safety: one central node can affect many downstream procedures. Check independent behavior, not just graph format.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Replacing a query node can change all downstream inputs. Despite editing one node, check whether its dependent routes still work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.09153-procedural-graphs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-36893bcf703a5f2a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:procedural-graphs" data-paper-title="Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6396bb67c386274">Does preserving the first and last nodes locally constitute full held-out capability verification?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprocedural-graphs">Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The local deterministic edit gate requires existing routes to retain endpoints and tests acceptance and rejection without real tools. It checks a structural condition but cannot establish semantic correctness of middle steps or generalization of the edited graph. The policy must not see hidden plans or answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A graph can retain start and end while deleting required authentication and still pass structurally. That contract cannot replace real task-success evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.09153-procedural-graphs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6396bb67c386274">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnesslens" data-paper-title="Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harnesslens-7d46fb0d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1bd6146aa60c6f88">Why does HarnessLens treat validation cost as a bottleneck for harness search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnesslens">Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fully running a fixed validation set for each candidate consumes many rollouts, and its mean can hide regressions in a few affected behaviors. HarnessLens focuses validation on behavior actually touched by a change, making evidence more targeted under a budget. State local coverage; saving evaluation does not justify skipping attribution or expanding quality claims.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rerunning every unrelated math problem after changing browser recovery can waste effort. Find matching behavior tasks, while noting that other behaviors have no new coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27311-harnesslens/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1bd6146aa60c6f88">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnesslens" data-paper-title="Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5970447fb917ddcb">Why is behavior-aware paired validation better than a fixed validation-set average at finding local regressions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnesslens">Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A change affects only some behaviors. Unrelated tasks dilute differences and waste rollouts. Compare parent and child on affected tasks and require attribution to the change, distinguishing actual repair from noise. State the scope of a local pass; one behavior&#x27;s improvement does not establish that every task improved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If only retry behavior changes, pair timeout and recovery tasks. Many easy successes could hide a retry loop in an overall mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27311-harnesslens/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5970447fb917ddcb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnesslens" data-paper-title="Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fec5db47abd72cf">How does passing a local behavior acceptance gate differ from proving overall agent improvement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnesslens">Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The local gate requires positive paired gains on target behavior and evidence they are attributable, answering whether the particular change is worth accepting for that behavior. Overall capability includes uncovered tasks, other behaviors, and resource effects. Neither Δ_b nor A_b generalizes automatically. Retain the validation set and change scope rather than relabeling a local pass as broad validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Improvements on five recovery cases can support limited acceptance. They do not show better code generation, mathematics, or all browsing tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27311-harnesslens/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fec5db47abd72cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnesslens" data-paper-title="Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aad409452ebef205">Why is A_b required in addition to Δ_b&gt;0?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnesslens">Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A positive difference may come from random retries or environmental changes; A_b requires evidence attributable to the candidate. The local project has a real tool-feedback protocol without answer/guide but did not run the paper&#x27;s four complete benchmarks. Local success cannot replace reported held-out gains, and structural labels do not prove causality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If two runs differ randomly and the candidate behavior was never checked for activation, do not credit the entire positive difference to the patch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27311-harnesslens/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aad409452ebef205">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jit-agent" data-paper-title="JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-jit-agent-92c11b63" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-22c8f75c233ddfc6">Why does Jit-Agent generate a workflow for the current task rather than choose only a fixed prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajit-agent">JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LV-NUS Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tasks need different memory, planning, action protocols, and tools. A universal harness can be heavy or lack key support. Jit-Agent composes a workflow when a task arrives so execution organization matches the request. Instant generation still needs quality constraints and frozen evaluation. Complete modules do not guarantee an advantage over fixed workflows.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One-step arithmetic may not need long-term memory, whereas organizing several pages can need evidence collection and progress tracking. Task features should guide which modules are used.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25593-jit-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-22c8f75c233ddfc6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jit-agent" data-paper-title="JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f7f1b4cdc3ad572">Why separate memory, planning, action protocol, and tools when generating a harness per task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajit-agent">JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LV-NUS Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Task bottlenecks vary by layer. Modules make proposals and repairs target the right object and let configuration archives yield transferable patterns. Just-in-time generation still needs validation; each module must meet its execution contract. Editing prompt text without generating matching tools or state interfaces does not implement all four modules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long task may need new memory, whereas short arithmetic needs only a calculation tool. Do not rebuild everything or mix incompatible protocols.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25593-jit-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6f7f1b4cdc3ad572">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jit-agent" data-paper-title="JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e2cd81f241f4787f">What are the trade-offs between on-demand generation and reusing one fixed harness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajit-agent">JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LV-NUS Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>On-demand configuration fits diverse tasks, and an archive can help transfer. Generation and repair add development cost and possible instability. A fixed harness is easier to maintain but can be overly generic. Count candidate generation and actual failures rather than cherry-picking the final successful configuration and ignoring exploration cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Long retrieval may need citation checking, whereas simple calculation may not. Task-specific generation distinguishes them, but an unnecessary checker may slow the easy task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25593-jit-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e2cd81f241f4787f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jit-agent" data-paper-title="JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7b9656fc577d1bd9">Why separate local training-time route repairs from frozen test execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajit-agent">JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LV-NUS Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training tasks can write repair experience. After freezing, validation and test use only public observations, tool metadata, and real feedback, not answers or reference plans. Report low controlled success rates and real ToolRoute results under their own protocols. Without the original model and full DeepSearchQA, do not import author scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A test error may be handled using a frozen recovery rule. Adding the hidden correct route to the archive and then calling it successful adaptation is invalid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25593-jit-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7b9656fc577d1bd9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:openloopevolve" data-paper-title="OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-openloopevolve-709aab65" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4968c00f9e6ec87b">Why is a Loop Policy more than a system prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aopenloopevolve">OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Observation, planning, memory, action, verification, and recovery assets jointly shape long-horizon behavior. Version both components and combinations. Prompt changes may miss the real bottleneck; executable versions, comparison, and monitoring make evolution traceable. Complete files do not imply effective behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A prompt may say &#x27;retry after failure,&#x27; but if recovery middleware cannot identify timeouts, the actual loop may still not recover.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.09380-openloopevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4968c00f9e6ec87b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:openloopevolve" data-paper-title="OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f68c8d27ea47fea">Why are release monitoring and rollback needed in addition to Champion–Challenger evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aopenloopevolve">OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An offline candidate that beats the champion may still be unstable after deployment or over long interactions. Monitoring must allow traceable restoration of the old version when regressions appear. Version observations, planning, memory, verification, and recovery assets rather than only model names. Release governance is part of the evolution loop, not replaced by one passing candidate test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A challenger saves calls during development but loops on permission errors in production. Monitoring should identify its version and roll back instead of allowing unbounded trial and error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.09380-openloopevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f68c8d27ea47fea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:openloopevolve" data-paper-title="OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f8d343b5c61d073">How does Champion–Challenger differ from overwriting the current policy each round?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aopenloopevolve">OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep the champion as a verified baseline, compare challengers before release, and roll back under runtime monitoring if needed. This reduces persistent contamination by unverified changes. A release gate needs actual evaluation and version evidence rather than favorable self-assessment; online monitoring does not authorize arbitrary external deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a recovery policy validates well but regresses after release, you should be able to restore a specific old version rather than having only an overwritten configuration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.09380-openloopevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8f8d343b5c61d073">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:openloopevolve" data-paper-title="OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<h2 id="qa-a5becae453b70928">Do local version and rollback states demonstrate real long-term online self-evolution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aopenloopevolve">OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic local PlanBench verifies mechanism branches, version state, and reporting, with no real browser, service, or YC-Bench. Proxy costs, release flags, and rollback counts are control evidence, not online risk or success metrics. Do not present the paper&#x27;s online or offline results as local measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rules can change a state from challenger to champion. Without running actual models and tools, this does not establish deployment of a stronger agent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<h2 id="qa-2476b944234ef8ff">Why does the four-stage loop put failure traces in the experiment knowledge base too?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx">AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Failures reveal implementation limits, guardrail risks, and unsupported hypotheses. Recording only successes creates survivorship bias and encourages repeated mistakes. Brainstorm, Developing, Evaluation, and SGPO connect evidence, code, online checks, and knowledge updates. Distinguish the authors&#x27; production system from local control flow.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a feature improves offline scores but hurts online latency, recording the failure and conditions can prevent repeating the high-risk proposal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26859">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2606.26859-agentx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2476b944234ef8ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentx" data-paper-title="AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<h2 id="qa-5c6f98a0c4e7b3e7">Why can a guardrail violation veto release after significant improvement in the primary metric?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx">AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recommendation systems must jointly satisfy target gains and key constraints. A single gain can come at the expense of stability or other important experience. The Evaluation Agent uses online evidence and guardrails to veto release, records both successes and failures, and learns from full traces rather than selecting winners and creating optimistic bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A higher click-through rate does not justify release if critical latency violates its limit. Record the failure cause for the next proposal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26859">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2606.26859-agentx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c6f98a0c4e7b3e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<h2 id="qa-594ae560d1f3665d">What conclusions do offline implementation checks and production A/B tests support in AgentX?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx">AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline checks find code, data, and runtime-contract problems before safe traffic exposure. Online A/B tests measure the primary metric and guardrails in a business environment. The tasks and risks differ, so offline success cannot replace release evaluation. Local small episodes or update counts are not the authors&#x27; production evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Unit tests can establish that recommendation code is ready for further experimentation. User behavior and latency effects require a controlled comparison on corresponding traffic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26859">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2606.26859-agentx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-594ae560d1f3665d">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<h2 id="qa-296e78851537b605">Do policy-update counts from 120 local episodes demonstrate large-model SGPO training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx">AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. They verify four-stage execution, asset management, and reuse without Kuaishou&#x27;s repositories, user traffic, or SGPO training. Average proxy cost is not human efficiency, revenue, or user time. Production gains are author-reported; deterministic perfect scores do not replicate industrial recommendation iteration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>108 experiment-knowledge reuses are a local workflow count. Without actual A/B tests, they cannot be converted to annual revenue or production value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scientist-one" data-paper-title="ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
