<span id="paper-agent-research-scientist-one-ba34af9f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0de4476b19cd6939">Why does Scientist-One make research claims independently traceable and checkable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascientist-one">ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Automated research can generate code, charts, and conclusions whose reported numbers lack actual execution or do not match source definitions. Scientist-One connects claims, evidence, and run records so readers can inspect their origin. This chain is an audit entry point, not proof by hash; still check contents, units, and experiment stage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An accuracy gain should trace to the corresponding split and run. Finding a hashed file does not show the value inside is accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26340">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2605.26340-scientist-one/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0de4476b19cd6939">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scientist-one" data-paper-title="ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0979e17fc2ce7849">Why check metric, stage, unit, and direction even when the source and logs exist?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascientist-one">ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A log can contain training, ablation, and formal evaluation values that are not interchangeable. Match each claim to evidence with consistent identity and protocol, then check recomputability and method–code consistency. Provenance rate is empty when there are no quantitative claims, not perfect. A source&#x27;s existence does not show it supports the claim.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A log may record lower training loss while a report claims higher test accuracy. Traceability to a number is not matching evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26340">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2605.26340-scientist-one/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0979e17fc2ce7849">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scientist-one" data-paper-title="ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d5ea75c7583ba81">Why are numeric CPR and scholarly citation authenticity different issues?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascientist-one">ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CPR checks whether quantitative claims trace to numerically matching execution logs with consistent metric, stage, unit, and direction. Citation verification separately requires retrieval and semantic disambiguation. A number can match while a citation is fabricated, and a real paper may not support the claim. Neither check replaces the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Training loss cannot support test accuracy even if the numbers happen to match. A real paper with the same title does not show it reported the claimed result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26340">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2605.26340-scientist-one/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d5ea75c7583ba81">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scientist-one" data-paper-title="ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-79ed0d4a52806e10">How should five zero-mean recomputations, no quantitative claims, and tied votes be handled?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascientist-one">ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>For a deterministic zero mean, require exact zero without a loose epsilon. CPR is null without quantitative claims, not perfect. No majority or abstention leaves the result unverified. I1 uses population standard deviation for tolerance. Trusted evaluation and log provenance are ensured upstream, and fixtures do not verify the whole study.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A draft with no numbers does not earn CPR=1 from a zero denominator. Opposing votes from two reviewers do not default to majority approval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26340">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2605.26340-scientist-one/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79ed0d4a52806e10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagents" data-paper-title="HyperAgents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-hyperagents-ae71283f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-42342c52c5c76f30">Why does HyperAgents edit both task solutions and the program that generates the next solution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagents">HyperAgents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed improver searches with the same proposal and reflection routines, whose limitations can block progress. HyperAgents makes the task and meta programs editable to study whether improvement methods evolve through experience. Self-modifying code is harder to validate; a new archived version does not establish actual performance or sustained gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one version always suggests similar changes, try editing the proposer itself. Then verify that the new proposer actually produces more effective candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.19461-hyperagents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-42342c52c5c76f30">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagents" data-paper-title="HyperAgents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1955136546ec1e42">Why does parent sampling consider both performance and existing offspring count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagents">HyperAgents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Selecting only top scores repeatedly expands the same branch and reduces diversity. Penalizing offspring count gives viable, less explored parents opportunities. Both the task agent and its modification mechanism are editable, allowing the improvement process itself to evolve. Sampling probability allocates budget; it does not accept every child or guarantee monotonic gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A champion with twenty children may get fewer chances than a slightly weaker parent tried once, opening other improvement paths rather than polishing one branch indefinitely.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.19461-hyperagents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1955136546ec1e42">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagents" data-paper-title="HyperAgents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6ebd187b8938135">How does fixing the meta-agent versus making it editable change the search space?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagents">HyperAgents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed improver generates variants only in the task-solution space. Editing the meta-agent can also change candidate generation and improvement procedures. The extra freedom adds failure and attribution challenges, requiring separate execution and evaluation. Local archive operations generate or run no arbitrary source, so lineage is not full program self-modification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing a sorting function is task-level. Changing how functions are selected for trials is meta-level, and the extra freedom may not help.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.19461-hyperagents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6ebd187b8938135">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagents" data-paper-title="HyperAgents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ccc25faa1e3c6fce">Does the local archive step execute model-generated source or shell commands?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagents">HyperAgents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It calculates parent distributions and maintains a bounded structured archive. Generated code and shell execution are prohibited, so the path does not validate self-referential program modification. Probabilities summing to one and correct lineage updates are search-control evidence, not task- and meta-agent behavior evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Editing one field tests the archive, but without running the changed program we cannot know whether it breaks the task or improves search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.19461-hyperagents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ccc25faa1e3c6fce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:polca" data-paper-title="POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-polca-3e1ab10b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0893e96060cf1920">Why does noisy optimization easily mistake a lucky high score for a good solution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apolca">POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin-Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Random batches, execution, and evaluation vary the score of one candidate. Keeping only observed maxima favors luck. POLCA uses evaluation history and global experience while limiting redundant proposals. More history does not eliminate bias: use consistent evaluation and budgets, and do not replace actual observations with expected outcomes of untested proposals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Configuration A may score high on an easy batch while B is stable across batches. Comparing only maxima can choose wrongly; keep full histories to check.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.14769">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.14769-polca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0893e96060cf1920">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:polca" data-paper-title="POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d412acefc26869b2">Why maintain a history-based mean and use a semantic epsilon-net to limit redundancy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apolca">POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin-Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Random data and evaluators introduce noise, so one high score may be accidental. Repeated observations stabilize candidate comparisons. Semantic distance constraints prevent budget waste on near-duplicates; recompute distances after adding candidates. Keep empirical-mean rules distinct from theoretical UCB, and don&#x27;t interpret rankings as statistical significance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Semantic filtering can avoid evaluating ten prompts differing only in punctuation. Combine a lucky first score with later evaluations rather than making it a permanent champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.14769">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.14769-polca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d412acefc26869b2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:polca" data-paper-title="POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-72aa3981c593eb47">Why distinguish empirical-mean priority in the POLCA main text from the theoretical UCB variant?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apolca">POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin-Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Empirical mean ranks candidates by their observed average reward; UCB explicitly adds an exploration bonus for uncertainty. They can prioritize rarely evaluated candidates differently and change budget use and selection history. Describe implementation and theoretical rules separately; properties do not transfer to an unimplemented variant by name.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A candidate evaluated once might not rank high by mean. UCB can give it another trial because uncertainty is high, producing a different next round.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.14769">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.14769-polca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72aa3981c593eb47">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:polca" data-paper-title="POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b232414eebadc9b4">How are untested proposals and observations completed before failure recorded after the metric budget is exhausted?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apolca">POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin-Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Charge each actual call before making it and keep observations completed before failure. Mark unevaluated proposals deferred_budget and omit them from observed-reward statistics. Old and new candidates use the same with-replacement batch. There is no mock LLM fallback; deep-copy callback inputs and outputs to protect history. Local tests do not demonstrate real generative optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the last budget evaluates one new proposal, the other three are neither zero scores nor default successes. They have no observations and must remain separate from evaluated candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.14769">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.14769-polca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b232414eebadc9b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mars-research" data-paper-title="MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-mars-research-5e806f85" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc84c4925aa29228">Why does Design–Split–Implement first produce a modular repository?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amars-research">MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Research changes touch several components. Defining design and module boundaries before implementation lets branches improve locally and reuse debugging experience instead of rewriting everything. Interfaces can still be incomplete; actual training establishes behavior, not tidy structure or small diffs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Separate loading, model, and evaluation so a branch can replace only the model under an unchanged evaluation entry point, without confounding data changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02660v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2602.02660-mars-research/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc84c4925aa29228">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mars-research" data-paper-title="MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c36b6b4056dd27e5">Why should research-search node value include both performance and runtime?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amars-research">MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Under a fixed training budget, an equally good but slower option crowds out later exploration. MARS normalizes execution metrics, adds a time penalty, and bounds improvement or debugging. Reflection uses code diffs and real results, not the model&#x27;s predicted performance in place of node measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If two options reach similar validation scores but one takes ten times longer, prioritize the faster one to test more structural hypotheses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02660v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2602.02660-mars-research/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c36b6b4056dd27e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mars-research" data-paper-title="MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-239f41d9330029f8">What do the new, improve, and debug search actions change?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amars-research">MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>New explores a different research proposal; improve builds on a valid node; debug repairs a candidate that cannot execute validly. They produce different evidence: fewer errors are not higher metrics, and executability does not justify more search. MARS selects by execution status and budget and caps debugging and descendants. Estimated scores for failures are not measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Debug an import error before measuring performance. Improve a valid but promising score; create a new branch to try a wholly different approach.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02660v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2602.02660-mars-research/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-239f41d9330029f8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mars-research" data-paper-title="MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6074a7a5727628e7">What boundaries apply to identical node metrics, debugging, and experience capacity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amars-research">MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If the metric range is zero, normalize to 0.5 rather than divide by zero. The paper caps search at ten debugging attempts, two improvement children, and thirty recent experiences. There is no local implementation or training. Author code and released traces do not establish a fully reproducible controller, and copying a reward formula is not research capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If all AUC values tie, do not produce NaN or assign an arbitrary candidate a very high score. The common midpoint leaves factors such as time active.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与成本判断. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02660v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2602.02660-mars-research/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6074a7a5727628e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:self-refine" data-paper-title="Self-Refine" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-self-refine-16be87c4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f58bee1c1db1b73e">Why treat an output as a draft that can be improved against specific requirements in Self-Refine?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aself-refine">Self-Refine</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Open-ended generation may require correctness, completeness, clarity, and style; one attempt may meet only some. Self-Refine generates, diagnoses shortcomings, and revises without extra parameter training. The loop needs actionable feedback, and mistaken feedback can make later drafts worse; more rounds do not imply better quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct first explanation lacks an example. Point out the gap before revising; &#x27;make it better&#x27; may not identify what to change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17651">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.17651-self-refine/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f58bee1c1db1b73e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:self-refine" data-paper-title="Self-Refine" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-439d518e3a48ecee">Why generate explicit feedback separately when the same model writes both draft and feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aself-refine">Self-Refine</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Explicit feedback converts unmet constraints into actionable edits, avoiding mere random resampling. Generation, feedback, and refinement play distinct roles, and stopping still depends on the model. No extra training does not make feedback correct, and repeated polishing is not independent fact-checking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A draft omits units. Feedback to add units to each number gives a concrete target that &#x27;write it better&#x27; does not.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17651">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.17651-self-refine/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-439d518e3a48ecee">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:self-refine" data-paper-title="Self-Refine" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-aafa2deef3b0dbdb">Compared with Reflexion&#x27;s cross-trial episodic memory, what loop does Self-Refine emphasize?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aself-refine">Self-Refine</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Self-Refine revises the current draft through feedback. Reflexion saves failure experience in bounded memory for a later trial. They can be combined but use different state. Refinement does not automatically form long-term memory, and repeated rewriting is not parameter RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Revising one email three times is Self-Refine. Saving &#x27;check recipients first&#x27; for tomorrow&#x27;s email involves cross-trial memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17651">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.17651-self-refine/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aafa2deef3b0dbdb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:self-refine" data-paper-title="Self-Refine" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d41641b7b845502f">Does stopping under a deterministic local critic demonstrate reliable real-LLM self-evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aself-refine">Self-Refine</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A controlled critic verifies generation, feedback, revision, and stopping states, without a general LLM or the seven original benchmarks. Stopping verifies the contract, not reliable recognition of factual correctness on open tasks. Local perfect scores cannot stand in for human preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rule can stop once text length is sufficient even when facts are wrong. Real self-assessment can be satisfied too early and needs independent evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17651">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.17651-self-refine/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d41641b7b845502f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:reflexion" data-paper-title="Reflexion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-reflexion-b837a66e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2a78cc6a61444ea4">Why does Reflexion retain failure lessons between attempts rather than just resample?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Areflexion">Reflexion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northeastern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Repeatedly trying the same task by resampling may repeat errors. Reflexion converts execution evaluation into readable experience so feedback survives across trials. Storing a lesson does not establish accuracy or transfer. Distinguish external reward from text reflection; neither automatically updates model weights with RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the first search stalls on an irrelevant page, reflection can advise checking sources and expanding the query. Restarting without the lesson can follow the same route.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.11366-reflexion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2a78cc6a61444ea4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:reflexion" data-paper-title="Reflexion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bb3bffbeb91462b9">Why is verbal reinforcement not reinforcement-learning updates to model parameters?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Areflexion">Reflexion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northeastern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Feedback becomes natural-language experience in bounded episodic memory. The next attempt sees a different context without gradient updates to weights. Reflection can communicate more than binary success but can be wrong. An Evaluator must still judge execution rather than treating reflection&#x27;s claims as learning evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Remember &#x27;check the file path before editing&#x27; after failure. Reading that note changes behavior next round even with identical weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.11366-reflexion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bb3bffbeb91462b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:reflexion" data-paper-title="Reflexion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6913428acdd0141">What does actionable reflection add over saving a binary failure reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Areflexion">Reflexion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northeastern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Binary reward only says the attempt failed. Reflection proposes a cause and actions to try or avoid, supplying actionable context. That inference may be wrong and needs actual next-trial feedback. Do not place the hidden reference plan into reflection and credit later success to autonomous learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>&#x27;Failure&#x27; does not locate the problem. &#x27;The date parameter needs ISO format&#x27; is useful, but must come from a visible error rather than a gold route.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.11366-reflexion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6913428acdd0141">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:reflexion" data-paper-title="Reflexion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cba650900339d0a3">Why interpret the mini-suite score of 0.9 separately from isolated ToolRoute results?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Areflexion">Reflexion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northeastern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The mini-suite deterministically fails the first attempt in each family and then reuses feedback, with fixed reflection templates and evaluator. ToolRoute is a different tool environment without a reference-policy interface. Neither is HumanEval pass@1. Bounded append and failure retention can be checked, but scores cannot rank across protocols or replace the paper.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One deliberately failed task in each of twelve families sets the aggregate rate, unlike natural model errors across 120 independent coding problems.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.11366-reflexion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cba650900339d0a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ruharness" data-paper-title="When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ruharness-cecd9850" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e575e0803773eb3">If an agent can already edit its harness, why update the rubric too?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aruharness">When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A repaired harness changes its failure distribution. Fixed criteria may track resolved faults and miss new ones. RuHarness reevaluates criteria against current trajectories while keeping the task objective fixed, then uses criteria that still diagnose weaknesses to guide edits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Initially it forgot search; later it searches but submits with insufficient evidence. Rewarding any search call misses the new failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36826v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.36826-ruharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2e575e0803773eb3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ruharness" data-paper-title="When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8cfddc49739eda77">Why compute discrimination, coverage and predictiveness from one six-cell posterior?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aruharness">When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They are correlated because they come from the same success/failure × Violated/Satisfied/N/A table. Add 0.5 to each cell, draw 2,000 joint Dirichlet samples, recompute all three for each draw and take the 0.2 utility quantile. Independent draws would discard correlations. Trajectory-set N and Red are fixed during sampling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two observed violations both fail, giving a high point estimate. A lower posterior quantile reflects that two hits are not hundreds of stable observations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与实现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36826v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.36826-ruharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8cfddc49739eda77">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ruharness" data-paper-title="When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-503b195db49bbbcd">Does better rubric compliance automatically promote the next harness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aruharness">When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Rubrics diagnose weaknesses and guide proposals, not task outcomes. Candidates must pass external verification and compete with the current harness on independent validation. Only the top-scoring candidate whose improvement strictly clears the threshold replaces it. Final test is excluded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A candidate adds many evidence-check lines but does not improve validation success. Keep the current harness rather than promote prettier self-check logs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与实现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36826v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.36826-ruharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-503b195db49bbbcd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ruharness" data-paper-title="When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3ad4f868d9fa0da1">Does outcome-blind judging conflict with later use of success/failure labels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aruharness">When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The judge sees behavior only when assigning rubric labels, avoiding hindsight. A separate statistical layer then joins those labels with outcomes to form the six-cell table. The component accepts both inputs but cannot prove an external judge was blinded or claim full evaluation integration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Seal the label for whether the target file was checked before revealing test success; don&#x27;t reinterpret an ambiguous check after learning the run failed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 数据协议与实现边界, 本地结果与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36826v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.36826-ruharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3ad4f868d9fa0da1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:crop" data-paper-title="CROP: Token-Efficient Reasoning in Large Language Models via Regularized Prompt Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-crop-02b87dce" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1abbf5985f2cce1c">Does CROP optimize model parameters, individual answers or the system prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acrop">CROP: Token-Efficient Reasoning in Large Language Models via Regularized Prompt Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It freezes model weights and iterates the system prompt offline. The model generates; task and length critics identify accuracy and redundancy problems; a meta-optimizer rewrites the prompt. Deployment uses the selected prompt for one generation. This is neither hard truncation nor RL weight updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Iteratively changing “explain every step” to “keep the combined calculation and remove repetition” is prompt optimization; cutting any reply after 50 tokens is not.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 原论文关键图. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14214v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.14214-crop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1abbf5985f2cce1c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:crop" data-paper-title="CROP: Token-Efficient Reasoning in Large Language Models via Regularized Prompt Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f7cafa9a397e5728">Why threshold the length critic, and how are the two textual gradients combined?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acrop">CROP: Token-Efficient Reasoning in Large Language Models via Regularized Prompt Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Section 3.3 runs length criticism only when generation strictly exceeds the threshold. Eq. 3 concatenates task critique, newline and length critique per sample for the meta-optimizer, rather than averaging numeric losses. Gradually remove narrative redundancy while keeping required calculations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Threshold 40 does not trigger at 40 tokens but does at 41. “Check unit conversion” and “remove the repeated intro” cannot be replaced by scalar 0.7.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与实现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14214v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.14214-crop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f7cafa9a397e5728">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:crop" data-paper-title="CROP: Token-Efficient Reasoning in Large Language Models via Regularized Prompt Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-45e2a0411f0723d5">What does CROP add beyond accuracy-only prompt tuning, and are token savings lossless?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acrop">CROP: Token-Efficient Reasoning in Large Language Models via Regularized Prompt Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It adds length feedback and selection by output-token cost. Table 3 includes accuracy drops: Gemini2Flash on ObjectCounting goes 96.0%→94.8% while mean tokens go 101.2→19.6. Report both sides of the tradeoff, not universal losslessness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: At equal 0.9 accuracy a 50-token prompt can beat a 100-token one. If the short prompt is less accurate, do not report only length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 论文离线与线上效果, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14214v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.14214-crop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-45e2a0411f0723d5">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:crop" data-paper-title="CROP: Token-Efficient Reasoning in Large Language Models via Regularized Prompt Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-029893dfd176215d">How does local selection avoid test data or a final unevaluated prompt, and what do callbacks establish?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acrop">CROP: Token-Efficient Reasoning in Large Language Models via Regularized Prompt Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Selection requires fixed validation revision/IDs matching the frozen CoT length baseline, disjoint training IDs, and no train/test scoring for selection. Each round validates the current prompt before proposing the next, so the final unevaluated one cannot win. Deterministic model/critic fixtures verify gating, concatenation and selection, not real LLM improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Measured A=0.8 and B=0.9; last proposal C has no validation. Return B, not newest C.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 数据协议与实现边界, 本地结果与负控, 高成本完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14214v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.14214-crop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-029893dfd176215d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evalalloc" data-paper-title="Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<span id="paper-agent-research-evalalloc-e28d06aa" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-475561c032d4eedb">If cheap search feedback is sufficient, why spend extra on final confirmation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevalalloc">Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Search needs comparable low-cost guidance; final selection must separate near-tied candidates. EvalAlloc uses sparse shared-core search and paired confirmation that reuses cache, with real observations for the final prefix rather than perpetual imputation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A predicted difference of 0.01 can guide exploration but should not decide the champion by itself.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evalalloc" data-paper-title="Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-acbbb6ce4a3b415b">Can partial credit 0.9 add 0.9 to an item&#x27;s acquisition success count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevalalloc">Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Acquisition counts only full credit a_i and uses a Beta posterior for conservative p(1−p) informativeness. Partial grades are not full successes there but remain scores for the response model. Mixing the stages changes the shared core.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ten 0.9 scores yield a=0, n=10, not a=9; 0.9 still enters model fitting and final scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地结果与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37276v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.37276-evalalloc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-acbbb6ce4a3b415b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evalalloc" data-paper-title="Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-19ec74cd1e637afe">Why aren&#x27;t equally sized independent random item sets equivalent to a shared core?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevalalloc">Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Common items supply paired covariance, helping when candidates agree on most items and set difficulty varies. Frozen item model and prior put successive generations on one scale. Refitting per candidate breaks comparability. This benefit depends on candidate correlation, not guaranteed variance reduction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A faces hard items and B easy ones. A common informative core is more comparable than merely requiring 60 items each.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与实现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37276v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.37276-evalalloc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-19ec74cd1e637afe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evalalloc" data-paper-title="Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd62ca40b7b37d16">Why retain the search-cache union and check candidate IDs in cross-fitting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevalalloc">Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Already executed cells need not be paid for again; fill missing common-prefix items and retain candidate-specific observations. Separate two-fold refit predictions prevent candidates from training their own correction. The correction is zero when all items are observed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Keep A&#x27;s cached item 4 even if prefix is 0/1/2. If a round needs four new cells and only three remain, reject the round; never read hidden complete scores to select a winner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与实现边界, 本地结果与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37276v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.37276-evalalloc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd62ca40b7b37d16">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

After a failure, should the system revise one prompt, save a lesson, or change the entire task workflow?

## Takeaway

Distinguish retrying the current answer, storing language experience across attempts, and changing tool orchestration or the harness. Reflexion saves feedback for the next attempt without updating weights. Full research systems also propose, implement, evaluate, and track lineage. Each change needs its own acceptance criteria; editing a workflow is not evidence of capability gains. CROP mutates the system prompt offline. EvalAlloc allocates evaluation across candidates and estimates fitness. Token objectives and evaluation-cell budgets are different mechanisms.

## Example

After forgetting to verify dataset versions, save the lesson in the next plan or add version and split checks to the workflow. Evaluate on tasks not used to make the change, compare success and calls to the old process, and report same-case recovery as such. It does not establish generalization.

## Common pitfall

Separate development feedback from held-out evaluation. Keep hidden answers and scoring plans out of the evaluated system. Papers like AgentX involve actual research or industrial loops; local mini-suites, callbacks, and references do not reproduce them. Do not reopen expensive closed runs merely because a paper is grouped under self-improvement.

## Reading order

Read Reflexion for cross-attempt experience, Self-Refine for revision within an attempt, and AgentX for the complete proposal–evaluation–workflow-update loop and the local subset.

1. [Reflexion](../../../../agent-research/2303.11366-reflexion/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366)
2. [Self-Refine](../../../../agent-research/2303.17651-self-refine/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17651)
3. [AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems](../../../../agent-research/2606.26859-agentx/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26859)

## Check your understanding

If we add a reminder to a prompt after one failure and weights stay unchanged, did the model learn through RL?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    No. The change is to prompting, memory, or execution. It may improve behavior, but report it at that layer and test on held-out tasks. Model training claims require collecting a learning signal and updating policy parameters.

</details>
